name: Masquelet induced-membrane technique (two-stage PMMA spacer then autograft)
company: Technique, not a product (PMMA spacer from any bone cement supplier; graft from RIA/iliac crest; extenders from any DBM or ceramic vendor)
composition: Stage 1: debridement, stabilization and a PMMA (often antibiotic-loaded) cement spacer that induces a vascularized, growth-factor-rich membrane over 4-8 weeks. Stage 2: spacer removal and filling of the membrane-lined cavity with morselized cancellous autograft, usually with extenders (allograft chips, DBM, beta-TCP) and sometimes rhBMP or BMAC.

regulatory.reference: Not a regulated product; each component carries its own clearance

challenge: Included at the requester's instruction as the autograft benchmark for segmental defects; it is a surgical technique and should not be counted as a product in market-size work.

applications.evidence_summary: Morelli 2016 systematic review and meta-analysis (17 papers, 427 adults): union achieved in the large majority, with infection eradication high but reinterventions common; results depend on defect size, infection and graft volume.
applications.caveats: Heterogeneous case series; no RCT versus bone transport; femur-specific subgroup small.

evidence.title: Masquelet technique: myth or reality? A systematic review and meta-analysis.
evidence.finding: Pooled adult long-bone series show high union and infection-eradication rates with frequent reinterventions; variants (graft type, spacer antibiotics) did not clearly change outcome.

bd.reimbursement: Two inpatient admissions, each bundled in its own MS-DRG; the second stage is often coded as a nonunion repair with bone graft.
bd.notes: For a biologics vendor the Masquelet second stage is the single largest per-case graft-volume opportunity in the femur (40-100 cc), which is why extenders and antibiotic-eluting fillers target it.

name: REGENETEN Bioinductive Implant
ownership_history: Developed by Rotation Medical (Plymouth, MN; Collagen Tendon Sheet K112423 cleared 2011, K122048 2013, K140300 2014); Smith+Nephew agreed to acquire Rotation Medical on 2017-10-23 ($125 million upfront plus up to $85 million contingent) and completed the acquisition on 2017-12-06. Smith+Nephew clearances K222501 (2023-05-11) and K242631 (2024-11-26).
composition: Bioabsorbable, highly porous bovine type I collagen sheet fixed over the bursal surface of the tendon with staples; induces a layer of new tendon-like tissue.

on_label_indications: management and protection of tendon or extra-articular ligament injuries in which there has been no substantial loss of tendon or ligament tissue (bioinductivity demonstrated for tendon only); the delivery system is indicated for arthroscopic delivery (K242631)

applications.evidence_summary: Sponsor-run prospective cohort of 115 full-thickness tears augmented at repair: supraspinatus thickness increased 12.5% (medium) and 17.1% (large) and radiographic retear was 11.5% in medium tears at 2 years (Bushnell 2022, PMID:35788057). Partial-thickness isolated bioinductive repair (n=33) showed tissue fill-in in 95-100% (Schlegel 2021, PMID:33220413). The sponsor's RCT in large/massive tears (NCT04450342, n=119) was terminated for a 'sponsor decision not related to safety' and the posted primary endpoint shows 6-month retear 57.1% (95% CI 41-72) augmented vs 50.0% (34-66) repair alone. A 2026 multicenter revision-repair cohort reported 28.6% retear at 12 months (Delgado 2026, PMID:40939824). A 400-patient global registry (NCT06857084) and an investigator RCT (NCT05439850, n=78) are ongoing.
applications.caveats: The only randomized data are unfavorable and unpublished; cohort data are company-funded with MRI surrogate endpoints; terminated trial NCT03734536 (partial-thickness, n=168) also has no publication found.
applications.challenge: A hiring manager will ask why the pivotal-style RCT was stopped and whether the candidate has read the posted results.

evidence.title: Prospective multicenter RCT of ARCR augmented with REGENETEN vs ARCR alone in large or massive full-thickness tears
evidence.finding: Terminated; posted 6-month retear 57.14% augmented vs 50.00% control; no statistical analysis posted.

evidence.title: Two-year outcomes with a bioinductive collagen implant used in augmentation of arthroscopic repair of full-thickness rotator cuff tears
evidence.finding: Retear 11.5% in medium tears at 2 years; tendon thickness increased.

evidence.title: Isolated bioinductive repair of partial-thickness rotator cuff tears using a resorbable bovine collagen implant: two-year outcomes
evidence.finding: Clinically and statistically improved ASES and Constant scores; MRI tissue fill-in in 95-100%.

bd.reimbursement: Rotator cuff repair is an ASC/HOPD procedure; the implant is packaged into the facility payment with no separate device code; Smith+Nephew has pursued a Category III CPT add-on code for bioinductive augmentation (status unverified).
bd.notes: Sold by Smith+Nephew sports-medicine reps, the same people who carry the company's bone-void and soft-tissue biologics; the commercial case rests on implant volume (tens of thousands per year, company claim) rather than randomized outcomes.

name: RIA 2 (Reamer-Irrigator-Aspirator) autograft harvesting system
ownership_history: Synthes product (first 510(k) K993335 on 2000-06-12); J&J since 2012; second-generation RIA 2 launched ~2017. Part of the orthopaedics business slated for separation (J&J announcement October 14, 2025).
composition: Single-pass intramedullary reaming head with integrated irrigation and suction that collects reamings and marrow from the femoral (or tibial) canal into a filter for use as autograft; not a biologic product itself.

regulatory.reference: K993335 (RIA System, 2000-06-12); K013527 (modification, 2001-12-21); K042899 (RIA System expanded indications, 2005-03-16); K111437 (RIA System expanded indications, 2011-08-10); applicant Synthes (USA) / Synthes (USA) Products LLC; product code HTO. No separate RIA 2 clearance appears under the name in openFDA.
on_label_indications: Intramedullary reaming with simultaneous irrigation and aspiration; harvested reamings may be used as autologous bone graft

applications.evidence_summary: Dawson 2014 RCT (133 patients with nonunion or segmental defect at 3 Level 1 centers): RIA graft united 82.1% versus 86.0% for iliac crest (not significantly different), yielded 37.7 cc versus 20.7 cc for anterior ICBG, harvested faster than posterior ICBG, and caused significantly less donor-site pain; $738 disposable offset by OR time for larger harvests.
applications.caveats: Synthes supplied RIA kits; 20 of 133 lost to follow-up; union slightly lower numerically with RIA.

applications.evidence_summary: RIA is the dominant graft source for Masquelet stage two in large defects because of volume (mean 37.7 cc, up to 90 cc).
applications.caveats: Risk of iatrogenic donor femur fracture and blood loss in the harvested femur.

applications.evidence_summary: RIA is the preferred large-volume autograft source for the Masquelet second stage; meta-analysis of 4,819 patients found RIA had less donor-site pain, fewer infections and adverse events than ICBG, while ICBG had a higher union rate.
applications.caveats: Union advantage for ICBG in the pooled data; RIA has its own femoral fracture and blood-loss risks.

applications.evidence_summary: Dimitriou 2011: complication rate 6% after RIA (233 patients) vs 19.4% after ICBG (6,449 patients).
applications.caveats: Historical, heterogeneous data.

evidence.title: The reamer-irrigator-aspirator as a device for harvesting bone graft compared with iliac crest bone graft: union rates and complications.
evidence.finding: Comparable union (82.1% vs 86.0%) and time to union; less donor-site pain and larger graft volume with RIA.

evidence.title: Complications following autologous bone graft harvesting from the iliac crest and using the RIA: a systematic review
evidence.finding: Complication rate 6% after RIA vs 19.37% after ICBG; anterior crest had more infection, hematoma and fracture; posterior more chronic pain and sensory disturbance.

evidence.title: Outcomes and complications of RIA versus iliac crest bone graft harvesting: systematic review and meta-analysis
evidence.finding: RIA: lower site pain, fewer infections and adverse events; ICBG: greater rate of bone union; no difference in VAS.

bd.reimbursement: Disposable cost bundled in the inpatient MS-DRG; CPT 20939 (bone marrow aspiration for bone grafting) and 20902 (bone graft, any donor area, major) describe the graft harvest, not the device.
bd.notes: RIA is the autograft benchmark that every femoral biologic must beat on cost and union; at roughly $700-800 per disposable (2014 figure) it is cheaper than a BMP kit and competitive with premium void fillers.

name: Traumacem V+ Injectable Bone Cement
ownership_history: Synthes product; J&J since 2012; part of the orthopaedics business J&J announced it will separate (October 2025).
composition: PMMA (polymethylmethacrylate) bone cement with radiopacifier, formulated for low-volume (up to ~6 mL) injection through a cannulated helical blade or lag screw into the femoral head. Not a resorbable or osteoconductive material.

regulatory.reference: K170802 (TRAUMACEM V+ Injectable Bone Cement; Synthes (USA) Products, LLC; decision 2017-09-28; product code LOD, 21 CFR 888.3027)
on_label_indications: Augmentation of the TFN-ADVANCED Proximal Femoral Nailing System through cannulated implants and instruments for patients with poor bone quality (e.g., osteoporosis)

challenge: This is PMMA, not a biologic. It is in the atlas because it is the only implant-augmentation material with a specific proximal-femur indication and a published RCT, and because it displaced the calcium phosphate cements that preceded it.

applications.evidence_summary: Multicenter RCT of PFNA with versus without PMMA augmentation (Kammerlander 2018, 223 patients 75+): no difference in Timed Up and Go (primary) or mobility; fewer implant-related revisions in the augmented arm (trend). A DePuy Synthes-funded German cost-effectiveness model (Joeris 2022) found augmentation dominant (saves ~EUR 50 and gains 0.01 QALY per patient).
applications.caveats: Primary endpoint negative; revision difference underpowered; AO/industry-supported trial; cost model is manufacturer-funded and German-payer based.

applications.evidence_summary: The PHILOS screw-tip cement augmentation studied in Europe uses this cement, but the only RCT (Hengg 2019, PMID:30805708; NCT01847508, AO-sponsored) was stopped early at 67 patients with mechanical failure 16.1% augmented vs 14.8% control (RR 1.09, p=1.0). A meta-analysis of 1 RCT plus 5 observational studies (n=541) found fewer implant-related complications with augmentation (10.4% vs 19.9%) but no functional difference (Lecoultre 2024, PMID:38589503).
applications.caveats: US label is hip-only; proximal humerus screw augmentation is off-label in the US. The RCT was underpowered and negative.

evidence.title: Cement augmentation of the Proximal Femoral Nail Antirotation (PFNA) - A multicentre randomized controlled trial.
evidence.finding: No difference in TUG at any time point; trend toward fewer implant-related reoperations with augmentation; no augmentation-related complications.

evidence.title: Cost-Effectiveness of Cement Augmentation Versus No Augmentation for the Fixation of Unstable Trochanteric Fractures.
evidence.finding: Markov model from the German payer perspective: Traumacem V+ augmentation dominant (cost saving, QALY gain).

evidence.title: Cement augmentation of the proximal humerus internal locking system in elderly patients: a multicenter randomized controlled trial
evidence.finding: Terminated early; no difference in mechanical failure at one year (16.1% vs 14.8%).

evidence.title: Cement augmentation for proximal humerus fractures: a meta-analysis of randomized trials and observational studies
evidence.finding: Overall complications 15.6% vs 25.4% (OR 0.54) favoring augmentation, driven by implant-related complications; no difference in reintervention or function.

evidence.title: PHILOS Augmented - a Multicenter Randomized Controlled Trial
evidence.finding: Primary endpoint radiographic mechanical failure in year one; completed 2017-11, no results posted.

bd.reimbursement: Bundled in MS-DRG 480-482 (hip and femur procedures except major joint); no separate payment. The economic argument to hospitals is avoided cut-out revisions, not reimbursement.
bd.notes: Tied to the TFN-Advanced nail by label, so it is a razor-blade add-on to the nail contract rather than a stand-alone biologic sale. Competes with Stryker Gamma3/Gamma4 and Smith+Nephew Intertan nails that lack a labeled augmentation cement in the US.

name: i-FACTOR Peptide Enhanced Bone Graft
ownership_history: Cerapedics (Westminster, CO), private; P-15 technology originally developed as PepGen P-15 (Dentsply/CeraMed) for dental use.
composition: P-15 synthetic 15-amino-acid collagen-mimetic peptide adsorbed onto anorganic bovine bone mineral (ABM), suspended in an inert hydrogel carrier (putty); must be placed inside an allograft bone ring with anterior plate

regulatory.reference: P140019 (approved 2015-11-03; received 2014-08-27; 14 supplements listed)
on_label_indications: Single-level ACDF C3-C4 to C6-C7 in skeletally mature patients with radiculopathy (with or without neck pain) or myelopathy from a single-level disc abnormality, after 6 weeks of conservative care, inside an allograft bone ring with supplemental anterior plate

applications.evidence_summary: FDA IDE RCT (Arnold 2016, n=319, single-blind, noninferiority to local autograft in a cortical ring allograft): 12-month fusion 88.97% vs 85.82%, composite overall success 68.75% vs 56.94% (p=0.038); 2-year fusion 97.3% vs 94.4% (Arnold 2018); 6-year post-approval follow-up met all four noninferiority endpoints with 99% vs 98.2% fusion (Arnold 2022).
applications.caveats: Sponsor-funded; control was local autograft in a ring, not iliac crest; overall-success superiority is a composite that is driven partly by NDI and reoperation components.

applications.evidence_summary: Lumbar use of the i-FACTOR putty is off-label in the US (it is CE-marked more broadly); the lumbar program was carried by the P-15L / PearlMatrix product instead.
applications.caveats: No US lumbar data for the original i-FACTOR formulation retrieved.

evidence.title: Efficacy of i-Factor bone graft versus autograft in ACDF: results of the prospective, randomized, single-blinded FDA IDE study
evidence.finding: Met all four FDA noninferiority endpoints at 12 months; overall success 68.75% vs 56.94% (p=0.0382).

evidence.title: i-Factor bone graft vs autograft in ACDF: 2-year follow-up of the randomized single-blinded FDA IDE study
evidence.finding: 2-year fusion 97.30% vs 94.44% (ns); overall success 69.83% vs 56.35% (p=0.03); reoperation 7.45% vs 10.53%.

evidence.title: Six-year follow-up of a randomized controlled trial of i-FACTOR versus local autograft in single-level ACDF
evidence.finding: Fusion 99% vs 98.2%; noninferior on all four co-primary endpoints at 72 months; secondary cervical surgery 18.9% vs 20.2%.

bd.reimbursement: Bundled in cervical fusion MS-DRGs 471-473 inpatient; outpatient ACDF packaged under the APC; no product-specific HCPCS. Physician +20930 bundled.
bd.notes: Cerapedics sells through a mix of direct reps and independent distributors (channel mix not disclosed in sources reviewed). Being one of only three PMA-approved spine bone grafts (with Infuse and PearlMatrix) is the core positioning against 361 cellular allografts.

name: Abaloparatide (Tymlos)
company: Radius Health (taken private by Gurnet Point Capital and Patient Square Capital in 2022)
composition: Synthetic PTHrP(1-34) analog, 80 micrograms daily subcutaneous injection; anabolic agent.

regulatory.reference: NDA 208743 (April 2017; postmenopausal osteoporosis); men with osteoporosis added December 2022
on_label_indications: Treatment of postmenopausal women with osteoporosis at high risk for fracture
Increase of bone density in men with osteoporosis at high risk for fracture

applications.evidence_summary: No human fracture-healing RCT located for abaloparatide in any femoral indication; use for AFF or nonunion is extrapolated from teriparatide and from preclinical data.
applications.caveats: No clinical evidence.

applications.evidence_summary: No fracture-healing trial.
applications.caveats: No clinical evidence.

applications.evidence_summary: No completed randomized fracture-healing trial located on PubMed or ClinicalTrials.gov; the only registered fracture-healing study (NCT04626141, geriatric distal femur fractures) was withdrawn with zero enrollment.
applications.caveats: Any claim that abaloparatide accelerates fracture healing in humans is unsupported.

evidence.title: Time to healing in supracondylar distal femur fractures in a geriatric population treated with abaloparatide (double-blind, placebo-controlled)
evidence.finding: Withdrawn before enrollment.

bd.reimbursement: Pharmacy benefit; prior authorization; brand-only (no generic).
bd.notes: Positioned for secondary fracture prevention after hip fracture in fracture-liaison services, not for healing.

ownership_history: Radius Health agreed on 2022-06-23 to be acquired by Gurnet Point Capital and Patient Square Capital (about $890 million including CVR); Tymlos NDA 208743 is listed under sponsor Radius in Drugs@FDA.
challenge: Path is NDA 208743 (schema now includes NDA).

pipeline.expected_milestone: None.

name: Romosozumab (Evenity)
composition: Humanized monoclonal antibody against sclerostin, 210 mg monthly subcutaneous for 12 doses; dual anabolic/antiresorptive.

regulatory.reference: BLA 761062 (April 2019)
on_label_indications: Treatment of osteoporosis in postmenopausal women at high risk for fracture (boxed warning for MI, stroke and cardiovascular death; not to be started within one year of a cardiovascular event)

challenge: Amgen ran the phase 2 hip-fracture healing trial and it was negative on every endpoint; romosozumab's tibial-fracture trial (not retrieved here) was also negative. The product's trauma relevance is nil beyond secondary prevention.

applications.evidence_summary: Schemitsch 2020 phase 2 RCT (n=332, intertrochanteric or femoral neck fractures after ORIF, 3 dose arms versus placebo): no difference in TUG (primary), time to radiographic healing (16.4-16.9 weeks in all arms) or RUSH score.
applications.caveats: Negative trial; sponsor-funded; dose-finding design.

applications.evidence_summary: Same trial (intertrochanteric fractures included); negative.
applications.caveats: Negative trial.

applications.evidence_summary: Amgen Phase 2 dose-finding RCT in 402 surgically fixed tibial diaphyseal fractures (nine romosozumab regimens vs placebo): no reduction in time to radiographic healing (JBJS 2020).
applications.caveats: Sponsor-funded; negative.

evidence.title: A Randomized, Placebo-Controlled Study of Romosozumab for the Treatment of Hip Fractures.
evidence.finding: Romosozumab did not improve fracture-healing-related clinical or radiographic outcomes versus placebo; safety comparable.

evidence.title: Romosozumab in Skeletally Mature Adults with a Fresh Unilateral Tibial Diaphyseal Fracture: A Randomized Phase-2 Study (J Bone Joint Surg Am 2020; DOI 10.2106/JBJS.19.01008)
evidence.finding: Median time to radiographic healing did not differ between romosozumab groups and placebo.

bd.reimbursement: Medical benefit (Part B, J3111) when administered in clinic, or pharmacy benefit; prior authorization; cardiovascular boxed warning limits use in the hip-fracture population.
bd.notes: Relevant to device BD only as evidence that pharmacologic 'healing acceleration' in hip fracture has failed in two well-run industry RCTs, which raises the bar for any device claiming the same.

ownership_history: Co-developed by Amgen and UCB; approved 2019.

pipeline.expected_milestone: None; fracture-healing development discontinued after the 2020 negative trials.

name: Teriparatide (Forteo; Bonsity and generics)
company: Eli Lilly (Forteo); Alvogen (Bonsity, 2019); multiple generics since 2023
ownership_history: Lilly launched Forteo in 2002; Alvogen's Bonsity (505(b)(2)) approved October 2019; Teva and others launched generics in 2023-2024 after patent expiry (dates not re-verified).
composition: Recombinant human PTH(1-34), 20 micrograms daily subcutaneous injection; anabolic agent.

regulatory.reference: NDA 021318 (Forteo; approved 2002-11-26; Drugs@FDA still lists it as an NDA - teriparatide is a 34-amino-acid peptide, below the 40-amino-acid threshold for the March 2020 BPCIA transition of protein products to BLAs). Alvogen Bonsity is NDA 211939.
on_label_indications: Treatment of postmenopausal women with osteoporosis at high risk for fracture
Increase of bone mass in men with primary or hypogonadal osteoporosis at high risk for fracture
Treatment of glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis at high risk for fracture

applications.evidence_summary: Bhandari 2016 (pooled Lilly phase 3 RCTs, n=159 of a planned 2,440): no difference in revision surgery, radiographic healing, pain or gait at 24 months.
applications.caveats: Severely underpowered after early termination; sponsor-funded.

applications.evidence_summary: Aspenberg 2016 / Malouf-Sierra 2017 (n=224, teriparatide versus risedronate started within 2 weeks of fixation of AO 31-A1/A2 fractures): faster TUG at 6-26 weeks, less pain after TUG, higher spine and femoral neck BMD at 78 weeks; no significant radiographic healing difference reported.
applications.caveats: Active comparator (risedronate may slow healing), BMD primary endpoint, Lilly-funded; only function and pain signals, not union.

applications.evidence_summary: Watts 2017 open-label prospective study (n=14): at 24 months 6 fractures healed, 3 partially, 2 unchanged, 1 nonunion; authors concluded teriparatide 'should not be relied on to aid in healing' of AFF. ASBMR 2013 task force: evidence 'inconsistent'.
applications.caveats: Tiny, uncontrolled; case reports dominate the rest of the literature.

applications.evidence_summary: One small open-label RCT in osteoporotic pubic-ramus fractures (Peichl 2011, PMID 21915572, n=65: 21 PTH 1-84 vs 44 control; healing 7.8 vs 12.6 weeks, 100% vs 9.1% healed at 8 weeks) and a planned Calgary phase 1/2 RCT (NCT06303284, n=54).
applications.caveats: PTH 1-84 (not teriparatide/PTH 1-34), unequal 1:2 allocation, open-label, single center, pubic rami only; PTH 1-84 is not marketed in the US.

applications.evidence_summary: Short pharmacologic note. Evidence for nonunion is case reports and small series: a 20-patient Italian multicenter series reported 85% of delayed/nonunions healed by 6 months of off-label teriparatide; a 40-patient comparative study of Ilizarov with or without teriparatide in septic tibial nonunion found shorter frame time. No RCT in established nonunion; the fracture-healing RCTs (distal radius, pelvis) showed modest or no effect on the primary endpoints.
applications.caveats: Off-label, osteosarcoma boxed-warning history (removed 2020), cost; outcomes in series are uncontrolled. Not a device-company product; relevant to BD as a prescribing trend that competes with surgical biologics in osteoporotic nonunion.
applications.challenge: Do not overstate; 'adjunct a surgeon might prescribe' is the honest framing.

applications.evidence_summary: Lilly-sponsored double-blind RCT of 102 postmenopausal women with non-operated distal radius fractures: median time to cortical bridging 9.1 weeks placebo, 7.4 weeks with 20 micrograms, 8.8 weeks with 40 micrograms; the prespecified primary comparison (40 micrograms vs placebo) was not significant (p=0.52) and the 20-microgram benefit was post hoc (Aspenberg 2010, PMID:19594305; NCT00190944). A blinded callus-quality substudy favored teriparatide (PMID:20367417). Pooled across 5 RCTs (n=380) teriparatide did not shorten radiographic healing (Shi 2016, PMID:27997614).
applications.caveats: Failed primary endpoint; sponsor-funded; surrogate radiographic outcome; cost and daily injection. A Chinese weekly-teriparatide RCT (NCT04473989, n=80) has unknown status.

evidence.title: Does Teriparatide Improve Femoral Neck Fracture Healing: Results From A Randomized Placebo-controlled Trial.
evidence.finding: No difference versus placebo in revision surgery, radiographic healing, pain control or gait speed at 24 months; trials terminated early for slow enrollment.

evidence.title: Effects of Teriparatide Compared with Risedronate on Recovery After Pertrochanteric Hip Fracture: Results of a Randomized, Active-Controlled, Double-Blind Clinical Trial at 26 Weeks.
evidence.finding: Teriparatide group completed TUG 3-6 seconds faster at 6-26 weeks and reported less pain after TUG; no between-group difference in most other endpoints.

evidence.title: Effect of Teriparatide or Risedronate in Elderly Patients With a Recent Pertrochanteric Hip Fracture: Final Results of a 78-Week Randomized Clinical Trial.
evidence.finding: Lumbar spine BMD +11.1% versus +6.5% and femoral neck +2.0% versus -1.2% with teriparatide; TUG faster through 26 weeks.

evidence.title: Responses to Treatment With Teriparatide in Patients With Atypical Femur Fractures Previously Treated With Bisphosphonates.
evidence.finding: BMD and turnover markers rose; no consistent effect on AFF healing (6 healed, 3 partial, 2 unchanged, 1 nonunion at 24 months).

evidence.title: Parathyroid hormone 1-84 accelerates fracture-healing in pubic bones of elderly osteoporotic women (J Bone Joint Surg Am 2011;93(17):1583-7)
evidence.finding: Prospective randomized open-label trial: 21 women received PTH 1-84 100 ug daily from within 2 days of admission vs 44 controls, all on calcium/vitamin D; CT-confirmed cortical bridging at 7.8 vs 12.6 weeks (p<0.001); at 8 weeks 100% vs 9.1% healed; VAS pain and Timed Up and Go improved.

evidence.title: Use of teriparatide in preventing delayed bone healing and nonunion: multicentric study on a series of 20 patients
evidence.finding: Off-label 6-month course with or without surgery; healing progression in 80% at 3 months and 85% healed at 6 months.

evidence.title: Effectiveness of teriparatide combined with the Ilizarov technique in septic tibial non-union
evidence.finding: Ilizarov with vs without teriparatide in ASAMI type C septic nonunions; teriparatide group had less time in frame (p<0.05); clinical outcome scores similar.

evidence.title: Teriparatide for acceleration of fracture repair in humans: a prospective, randomized, double-blind study of 102 postmenopausal women with distal radial fractures
evidence.finding: Primary 40-microgram comparison not significant; post hoc 20-microgram group bridged 1.7 weeks earlier.

evidence.title: Effectiveness of teriparatide on fracture healing: a systematic review and meta-analysis
evidence.finding: No significant effect on time to radiographic healing, healing rate or pain; function improved.

evidence.title: Teriparatide improves early callus formation in distal radial fractures (Acta Orthop 2010; DOI 10.3109/17453671003761946)
evidence.finding: Blinded qualitative callus scoring at 5 weeks in a single-center subset of the Aspenberg trial suggested richer early callus with teriparatide.

evidence.title: Effectiveness of Weekly Teriparatide Injection in Postmenopausal Patients with Hip Fractures (Clin Orthop Surg 2023; DOI 10.4055/cios22280)
evidence.finding: Double-blind RCT of weekly teriparatide vs saline after hip fracture (Korea); bone turnover and radiographic union assessed (result not extracted from abstract in this review).

bd.reimbursement: Outpatient pharmacy benefit (Medicare Part D / commercial formulary), typically with prior authorization and a 2-year lifetime limit historically (now relaxed); not a device line item. Inpatient initiation is absorbed into the DRG.
bd.notes: Generic entry has collapsed the price; for a device company the relevance is as a co-prescribed adjunct in fracture-liaison programs, not as a product. Off-label promotion for fracture healing is a compliance line no manufacturer crosses after the Norian and OP-1 cases.

challenge: Path is NDA (schema now includes NDA): teriparatide is a 34-amino-acid peptide regulated as a drug (generics via ANDA/505(b)(2)), not a biologic.

pipeline.expected_milestone: No sponsor is pursuing a fracture-healing label; ongoing investigator-initiated trials (e.g., tibial stress fracture in military trainees, NCT04589819, n=183, primary completion Dec 2026).

name: Zoledronic acid 5 mg (Reclast; generics)
composition: Intravenous nitrogen-containing bisphosphonate, 5 mg once yearly.

regulatory.reference: NDA 021817 (Reclast; osteoporosis 2007). The hip-fracture indication derives from HORIZON-RFT.
on_label_indications: Treatment and prevention of postmenopausal osteoporosis
Treatment to increase bone mass in men with osteoporosis
Treatment and prevention of glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis
Treatment of Paget's disease of bone
Reclast label includes reduction of new clinical fractures in patients with a recent low-trauma hip fracture

challenge: Path is NDA 021817 (Reclast; Drugs@FDA/openFDA currently lists the sponsor as Sandoz) - a small-molecule drug, not a biologic. Timing question: HORIZON-RFT dosed within 90 days of surgery and a post hoc analysis suggested the mortality and fracture benefit was greater when infusion was given at least 2 weeks after repair; no RCT shows that bisphosphonates impair hip fracture union.

applications.evidence_summary: HORIZON Recurrent Fracture Trial (Lyles 2007, n=2,127, first infusion within 90 days of hip fracture surgery): new clinical fractures 8.6% versus 13.9% (35% reduction) and all-cause mortality 9.6% versus 13.3% (28% reduction) over a median 1.9 years. Post hoc analyses show benefit regardless of baseline BMD.
applications.caveats: Novartis-funded; about secondary fracture prevention and mortality, not healing of the index fracture; benefit appears larger with infusion 2 or more weeks after surgery (post hoc).

applications.evidence_summary: Same trial (both femoral neck and trochanteric fractures enrolled).
applications.caveats: As above.

applications.evidence_summary: Bisphosphonates are stopped, not started, after an AFF; listed to make the contraindication explicit.
applications.caveats: Contraindicated in practice.

evidence.title: Zoledronic acid and clinical fractures and mortality after hip fracture.
evidence.finding: Yearly zoledronic acid after hip fracture repair reduced new clinical fractures by 35% and all-cause mortality by 28%.

evidence.title: Zoledronic acid reduces the rate of clinical fractures after surgical repair of a hip fracture regardless of the pretreatment bone mineral density.
evidence.finding: Post hoc HORIZON-RFT analysis: antifracture efficacy unchanged by baseline femoral neck or total hip BMD.

bd.reimbursement: Medical benefit: HCPCS J3489 (zoledronic acid, 1 mg) under Medicare Part B when infused in hospital outpatient or clinic; inpatient infusion is bundled in the DRG. Generic pricing makes it the cheapest post-hip-fracture intervention with mortality data.
bd.notes: The one pharmacologic adjunct that fracture-liaison services and hip-fracture co-management pathways (AAOS/AOA Own the Bone) treat as standard; device companies selling hip nails increasingly bundle 'bone health' messaging around it.

name: Infuse Bone Graft (rhBMP-2/ACS)
ownership_history: Developed by Genetics Institute/Wyeth (rhBMP-2) and Sofamor Danek; Medtronic acquired Sofamor Danek in 1999 and has held the spine franchise since. Wyeth's rights passed to Pfizer; Medtronic holds the spine/orthopedic franchise.
composition: Recombinant human BMP-2 (1.5 mg/mL) reconstituted onto an absorbable bovine type I collagen sponge; sold in kit sizes (XX-small through large) with a mandated Medtronic interbody device for spine use

regulatory.reference: P000058 (spine, approved 2002-07-02); P000054 (open tibial shaft fracture); P050053 (oral-maxillofacial); TLIF supplement P000058/S096 approved 2026-02-13 (one or two adjacent levels, L2-S1)
on_label_indications: Single-level ALIF L2-S1 with LT-Cage, Inter Fix, Inter Fix RP, Perimeter or Divergence-L (DDD, up to Grade I spondylolisthesis/retrolisthesis)
Single-level OLIF25 L2-L5 with Clydesdale or Pivox; single-level OLIF51 L5-S1 with Perimeter or Divergence-L (approved Dec 2015 and Apr 2018)

One or two adjacent levels L2-S1 by TLIF, with an FDA-cleared interbody fusion device and a metallic screw-and-rod system, for symptomatic DDD confirmed by history and radiographic studies after at least six months of nonoperative treatment (P000058/S096, Panel-Track supplement approved 2026-02-13; Breakthrough Device designation 2024-04-06)
Acute open tibial shaft fracture with IM nail within 14 days
Sinus augmentation; localized alveolar ridge augmentation for extraction-socket defects

applications.evidence_summary: Pivotal RCT (Burkus 2002, n=279) with LT-Cage: 94.5% fusion vs 88.7% ICBG at 24 months with similar clinical outcomes; YODA IPD meta-analysis confirmed a 12% higher fusion rate but clinically trivial ODI benefit and a nonsignificant retrograde ejaculation signal in ALIF.
applications.caveats: All RCTs sponsor-funded; YODA reanalyses (Fu 2013, Simmonds 2013) found selective reporting in the original publications.

applications.evidence_summary: On-label for single-level OLIF25/OLIF51 with named Medtronic cages via PMA supplements (2015, 2018); approval rested on existing ALIF data and device equivalence rather than a new lateral RCT.
applications.caveats: No published lateral-specific RCT located; the 2015/2018 supplements were based on prior Infuse data.

applications.evidence_summary: Pivotal RCT NCT04073563 (n=493 randomized 1:1:1 to Infuse 2.1 mg/level, 4.2 mg/level or local autograft; Bayesian adaptive design) met primary endpoints for both dose arms at first interim analysis; Medtronic reports >90% fusion in single-level TLIF. Historically off-label TLIF use was the largest rhBMP-2 use case and carried radiculitis/ectopic bone/osteolysis concerns (Carragee 2011); the earlier PLIF IDE (NCT01491464) was terminated.
applications.caveats: Full results not yet published as of this review; numbers come from the February 2026 press release and sponsored coverage. Two-level fusion numbers reported only as 'up to 87%'.

applications.evidence_summary: Dimar 2009 RCT (n=463) used rhBMP-2 on a compression-resistant matrix (the 'Amplify' formulation, never approved): 96% vs 89% fusion and fewer nonunion reoperations; Glassman 2008 RCT in patients over 60 (n=102) found fewer complications and revisions with rhBMP-2/ACS than ICBG. Posterolateral use of the marketed ACS product remains off-label.
applications.caveats: Amplify (rhBMP-2/CRM) received a non-approvable decision in 2011 amid cancer-signal concerns; the YODA cancer analysis (RR 3.45 at 24 months, low event counts) and 15-20% early back/leg pain events (Carragee) are the standing objections.

applications.evidence_summary: ISSG registry: rhBMP-2 used in 73.9% of 1,180 ASD patients (2008-2018), mean 23.6 mg; revision for pseudarthrosis 8.6% with BMP vs 17% without (Jain 2020); Maeda 2009 single-center comparison 4.3% vs 28.1% pseudarthrosis. All off-label and high-dose.
applications.caveats: Observational, industry-supported registry; dose per patient far exceeds any labeled dose.

applications.evidence_summary: FDA Public Health Notification (2008) warned of life-threatening neck/airway swelling with off-label cervical rhBMP; Smucker 2006 found clinically significant swelling in 27.5% vs 3.6%; Cahill 2009 (NIS) found higher wound and dysphagia complications. Medtronic's own single-arm cervical pivotal (NCT00485173, n=224 vs 486 historical controls) reported 99.4% fusion and 80.9% overall success but ossification in the target region in 78.6%; no cervical approval was granted.
applications.caveats: Not approved; FDA position is that safety and efficacy in the cervical spine have not been demonstrated.

applications.evidence_summary: The only level I evidence is the BESTT trial in open TIBIAL fractures (Govender 2002, n=450): 1.5 mg/mL rhBMP-2 reduced secondary interventions for delayed union by 44% and infections in grade III wounds. No femoral RCT exists.
applications.caveats: Off-label in the femur; tibial data; sponsor-funded; later FDA-mandated analyses of reamed-nail subgroups were less favorable.

applications.evidence_summary: Case series of rhBMP-2 in aseptic nonunion revision; no controlled femoral data.
applications.caveats: Off-label; cost ($3,000-5,000 per kit, public list price not verified) is bundled into the DRG.

applications.evidence_summary: Used by some centers inside the Masquelet membrane; animal data suggest the membrane may blunt BMP effect; no RCT.
applications.caveats: Off-label; heterotopic ossification and seroma reported in high-dose use.

applications.evidence_summary: BESTT (Govender 2002, n=450) found the 1.50 mg/mL dose reduced secondary interventions and infection in open tibial fractures with IM nails; the pooled subgroup analysis (n=510) localized the benefit to Gustilo IIIA/IIIB fractures and found none with reamed nailing. A later sponsored RCT with reamed nails (Aro 2011, n=277) showed no acceleration and a non-significant infection excess (19% vs 11%).
applications.caveats: Sponsor-funded; the label was built on a mostly unreamed-nail cohort while US practice is reamed nailing; FDA panel in 2004 argued for limiting use to 'problem' fractures. No public 2024-2026 trauma sales data; a trauma biologics manager will note most Infuse revenue is spine.
applications.challenge: Reamed-nail RCT (Aro 2011) failed its primary endpoint, so on-label use in the modern reamed-nail standard is on contested ground.

applications.evidence_summary: rhBMP-2 on an injectable calcium phosphate matrix in closed tibial fractures (Lyon 2013, n=369) was terminated at interim analysis for no effect on time to union; the CPM formulation was never commercialized.
applications.caveats: Negative RCT; not an indication.

applications.evidence_summary: Off-label use in nonunion rests on case series (e.g., prospective rhBMP-2/HA series 2024; Pakistani audit n=62) and a 2025 network meta-analysis that pools BMP RCTs mostly from the OP-1 era; no US RCT of Infuse in nonunion.
applications.caveats: Off-label; payer policies (e.g., Medica) list other long-bone uses as investigational and not covered.

applications.evidence_summary: DeVries 2012 (PMID 22575061): 23 revision TTC fusions with a retrograde nail, 7 with rhBMP-2 and 16 without; stable functional limb in 71.4% vs 68.8%, no difference in complications or time to union.
applications.caveats: Off-label; FDA labeling does not cover any foot or ankle use. Tiny comparison, retrospective, underpowered.

applications.evidence_summary: Bibbo 2009 (PMID 19589304): 69 patients, 112 high-risk ankle and hindfoot fusion sites (64% smokers, 32% talar AVN) treated with rhBMP-2; 96% union at a mean 11 weeks by CT, 4% nonunion, one deep infection.
applications.caveats: Single-surgeon retrospective series without controls; off-label use; the 2014 review by the same group states rhBMP-2 outside spinal fusion is FDA off-label and should be reserved for high-risk patients.

applications.evidence_summary: Used off-label by some Charcot surgeons; no comparative series found in this sweep.
applications.caveats: Off-label; cost and heterotopic bone and seroma concerns from the spine literature carry over.

applications.evidence_summary: Entirely off-label in the upper extremity. A 2024 systematic review and meta-analysis of 18 studies (16 pooled) found no significant improvement in humerus nonunion healing with rhBMP plus graft vs graft alone and a trend toward more infection (Alhakbani 2024, PMID:39429996). rhBMP-7 added to revision of 22 humeral nonunions made no difference (Hackl 2017, PMID:28784168). Local soft-tissue swelling after rhBMP-2 in a humeral nonunion has been reported (PMID:27299059).
applications.caveats: No RCT in any upper-extremity site; heterogeneous retrospective data; cost (thousands of dollars per kit) is hard to justify against 93-98% union with plate and autograft.

applications.evidence_summary: The only BMP RCT in the wrist used rhBMP-7 (OP-1), not Infuse: 17 proximal-pole nonunions randomized to iliac autograft, autograft plus OP-1, or allograft plus OP-1; OP-1 shortened radiographic healing from 9 to 4 weeks and let allograft match autograft (Bilic 2006, PMID:16506027).
applications.caveats: n=17, single center, product withdrawn from the US market; not transferable to rhBMP-2 dosing.

applications.evidence_summary: Wyeth ran a phase 1 dose-escalation of rhBMP-2 on a calcium phosphate matrix injected into closed distal radius fractures (NCT00161629, n=40, completed 2005-2007); no efficacy program followed.
applications.caveats: Abandoned development path.

applications.evidence_summary: Pivotal 21-center RCT (Triplett 2009, n=160, under 6 mm residual bone): mean bone height gain 7.83 mm with rhBMP-2/ACS versus 9.46 mm with autograft, denser induced bone, 199 of 241 versus 201 of 251 implants integrated and loaded at six months, 79 percent subject success, no rhBMP-2-related adverse events, and 17 percent long-term donor-site morbidity in the autograft arm; phase II dose-ranging RCT (Boyne 2005, n=48) preceded it. This is the only on-label growth factor anywhere in the craniomaxillofacial skeleton.
applications.caveats: Sponsor-run; height gain was lower than autograft; adding rhBMP-2/ACS to Bio-Oss reduced new bone in a separate RCT (PMID 22254226); a 2019 meta-analysis found the labeled 1.5 mg/mL dose gives orofacial gains similar to but not better than conventional grafts (PMID 31147568).

applications.evidence_summary: Six RCTs and two non-randomized studies (2025 meta-analysis, PMID 40003593) and earlier meta-analyses find bone volume equivalent to iliac crest (about 61 vs 59 percent), lower bone height, shorter operations and stays, and significant facial swelling in up to 37.5 percent (Alonso 2010 RCT, n=16); a 2021 umbrella review rated all included reviews at uncertain or high risk of bias. A US RCT of DBM/BMP versus ICBG with a cost primary endpoint (NCT04234971, n=40, UT Houston) is recruiting to 2028.
applications.caveats: Off-label in children; CHLA retrospective of 93 grafts shows 65 percent failure above an 885 mm3 cleft volume; long-term craniofacial growth data lacking.

applications.evidence_summary: Herford and Boyne 2008: 14 continuity defects after tumor or osteomyelitis regenerated with 4 to 8 mg rhBMP-2 on collagen alone under a tented titanium bar or mesh, all restored to prosthetic function; Carter 2008: 2 of 4 continuity defects failed and needed iliac crest. A 2019 safety review (PMID 31592029) concluded the evidence fails to support rhBMP-2 for mandibular reconstruction, calvarial reconstruction or distraction.
applications.caveats: Off-label; no controlled study; the label contraindicates use near a resected tumor, which is the usual mandibular indication.

applications.evidence_summary: Only case-level data for defect fractures and nonunion within the Carter 2008 series.
applications.caveats: Off-label.

applications.evidence_summary: Retrospective cohorts and case reports only for calvarial defects; two pediatric calvarial studies in the 2026 systematic review of 21 rhBMP-2 craniofacial studies (PMID 41944755).
applications.caveats: Off-label; heterotopic bone and swelling risk near dura and scalp.

evidence.title: Anterior lumbar interbody fusion using rhBMP-2 with tapered interbody cages
evidence.finding: 24-month fusion 94.5% rhBMP-2 vs 88.7% ICBG; 32% of ICBG patients had graft-site discomfort at 24 months.

evidence.title: Clinical and radiographic analysis of an optimized rhBMP-2 formulation as an autograft replacement in posterolateral lumbar spine arthrodesis
evidence.finding: rhBMP-2/CRM 96% vs ICBG 89% fusion at 24 months; nonunion failures 6 vs 18; 60% of ICBG patients reported donor-site pain at 24 months.

evidence.title: RhBMP-2 versus iliac crest bone graft for lumbar spine fusion: a randomized, controlled trial in patients over sixty years of age
evidence.finding: 20 complications with ICBG vs 8 with rhBMP-2/ACS; revisions for nonunion 5 vs 1; better CT fusion grade with rhBMP-2.

evidence.title: Effectiveness and harms of recombinant human bone morphogenetic protein-2 in spine fusion: a systematic review and meta-analysis (YODA)
evidence.finding: Lumbar fusion: rhBMP-2 and ICBG similar in overall success and fusion; cancer RR 3.45 at 24 months on low event counts; early industry publications misrepresented harms through selective reporting.

evidence.title: Safety and effectiveness of rhBMP-2 for spinal fusion: a meta-analysis of individual-participant data (YODA)
evidence.finding: At 24 months ODI 3.5 points better and radiographic fusion 12% higher with rhBMP-2 than ICBG; more early postoperative pain; cancer RR 1.98, inconclusive.

evidence.title: A critical review of rhBMP-2 trials in spinal surgery: emerging safety concerns and lessons learned
evidence.finding: Industry-sponsored publications reported 0% rhBMP-2-related adverse events in 780 patients; FDA summaries and later data suggest 10-50% event rates depending on approach; the 2011 Spine Journal issue that triggered the YODA reanalyses.

evidence.title: Prevalence, complications, and hospital charges associated with use of bone-morphogenetic proteins in spinal fusion procedures
evidence.finding: BMP use rose from 0.69% of fusions (2002) to 24.89% (2006); anterior cervical use associated with more complications (7.09% vs 4.68%) and dysphagia/hoarseness; charges 11-41% higher.

evidence.title: Increased swelling complications associated with off-label usage of rhBMP-2 in the anterior cervical spine
evidence.finding: Clinically significant prevertebral swelling in 27.5% with rhBMP-2 vs 3.6% without.

evidence.title: Pivotal clinical investigation of INFUSE with a PEEK interbody spacer and anterior cervical plate (single level)
evidence.finding: Posted results: overall success 80.9% vs 59.9% propensity-matched historical control; fusion 99.4% vs 87.2%; ossification in target region 78.6% vs 59.2%; no cervical approval followed.

evidence.title: Prospective, randomized, controlled, blinded pivotal study of Infuse in one- or two-level TLIF
evidence.finding: Three-arm RCT (2.1 mg/level, 4.2 mg/level, local autograft) stopped for success at first interim analysis; supported panel-track PMA supplement approved 2026-02-13. Results unpublished.

evidence.title: Use of rhBMP-2 for adult spinal deformity surgery: patterns of usage and changes over the past decade (ISSG)
evidence.finding: rhBMP-2 used in 73.9% of ASD patients, mean dose 23.6 mg and falling over time.

evidence.title: Cost-utility analysis of rhBMP-2 use in adult spinal deformity surgery
evidence.finding: Revision for symptomatic pseudarthrosis 8.6% with BMP vs 17% without; mean BMP cost $14,000 per index surgery.

evidence.title: FDA Public Health Notification: Life-threatening Complications Associated with Recombinant Human Bone Morphogenetic Protein in Cervical Spine Fusion
evidence.finding: At least 38 MDR reports in four years of neck/throat swelling with airway or neurological compression after cervical rhBMP use, most 2-14 days post-op; FDA states safety and effectiveness in the cervical spine have not been demonstrated and recommends approved alternatives or enrollment in approved studies.

evidence.title: Recombinant human bone morphogenetic protein-2 for treatment of open tibial fractures: a prospective, controlled, randomized study of four hundred and fifty patients (BESTT).
evidence.finding: 1.5 mg/mL rhBMP-2 group had a 44% reduction in risk of secondary intervention for delayed union (RR 0.56), fewer invasive interventions and faster healing than IM nail alone.

evidence.title: rhBMP-2 in open tibial fractures: a subgroup analysis of data combined from two prospective randomized studies
evidence.finding: In Gustilo IIIA/IIIB fractures (n=131) rhBMP-2 reduced bone-grafting (p=0.0005), invasive secondary interventions (p=0.0065) and infection (p=0.0234); in the reamed-nail subgroup (n=113) no difference.

evidence.title: rhBMP-2: a randomized trial in open tibial fractures treated with reamed nail fixation
evidence.finding: Healing 60% vs 48% at 13 weeks (p=0.054) and 68% vs 67% at 20 weeks; secondary procedures 12% in each arm; infection 19% vs 11% (p=0.065). Primary endpoint not met.

evidence.title: rhBMP-2/calcium phosphate matrix for closed tibial diaphyseal fracture: double-blind RCT phase II/III
evidence.finding: Terminated at interim analysis; median time to union 13.1 weeks (control) vs 13.0 and 15.9 weeks (rhBMP-2/CPM 1.0 and 2.0 mg/mL); no benefit.

evidence.title: rhBMP-2 combined with autologous bone for long bone nonunion: prospective case series
evidence.finding: rhBMP-2 on HA granules mixed 1:1 with autograft (max 6 mg) in nonunion and FRI defects; single-center outcome series, n not stated in abstract.

evidence.title: Recombinant bone morphogenetic protein-2 (rhBMP-2) in high-risk ankle and hindfoot fusions
evidence.finding: 96% union across 112 fusion sites in high-risk patients; 5 of 112 joints did not unite.

evidence.title: The effect of recombinant bone morphogenetic protein-2 in revision tibiotalocalcaneal arthrodesis
evidence.finding: No statistically significant difference in salvage or complications with rhBMP-2 in revision TTC nailing.

evidence.title: Bone morphogenetic proteins: indications and uses
evidence.finding: Narrative review: only a few foot/ankle BMP studies exist; rhBMP-2 is off-label outside spine and should be used only in high-risk patients.

evidence.title: Healing of humerus non-union fracture using rhBMP with bone graft compared to bone graft alone: systematic review and meta-analysis
evidence.finding: Pooled OR for union 0.65 (95% CI 0.07-6.38), not significant; infection rate OR 1.18, not significant; no RCTs available.

evidence.title: Long-term outcome following additional rhBMP-7 application in revision surgery of aseptic humeral, femoral, and tibial shaft nonunion
evidence.finding: 102 of 112 nonunions (19 of 22 humeral) healed within 12 months regardless of rhBMP-7; no difference in DASH.

evidence.title: Osteogenic protein-1 (BMP-7) accelerates healing of scaphoid non-union with proximal pole sclerosis
evidence.finding: OP-1 reduced radiographic healing time to 4 weeks vs 9 weeks with autograft alone.

evidence.title: Recombinant human BMP-2 and allograft compared with autogenous bone graft for reconstruction of diaphyseal tibial fractures with cortical defects (BESTT-ALL)
evidence.finding: Lower-limb reference trial: rhBMP-2 plus allograft matched autograft for tibial defects; cited when surgeons extrapolate to the humerus.

evidence.title: Phase 1 dose-escalating study of rhBMP-2/calcium phosphate matrix as adjuvant therapy for closed distal radius fractures
evidence.finding: Safety/feasibility only; no results posted.

evidence.title: Pivotal, randomized, parallel evaluation of rhBMP-2/ACS and autogenous bone graft for maxillary sinus floor augmentation
evidence.finding: rhBMP-2/ACS gave 7.83 mm versus 9.46 mm height with autograft, denser bone, equivalent implant integration (199/241 vs 201/251) at six months after loading, no treatment-related adverse events, and avoided the 17 percent donor-site morbidity of autograft.

evidence.title: De novo bone induction by rhBMP-2 in maxillary sinus floor augmentation (phase II)
evidence.finding: 0.75 and 1.50 mg/mL rhBMP-2/ACS produced ridge height gains of 9.5 and 10.2 mm versus 11.3 mm with bone graft at four months; 1.5 mg/mL chosen for the pivotal trial.

evidence.title: The negative effect of combining rhBMP-2 and Bio-Oss on bone formation for maxillary sinus augmentation
evidence.finding: Histologic new bone was lower with rhBMP-2/ACS plus Bio-Oss than with Bio-Oss alone.

evidence.title: Efficacy of rhBMP-2 and rhPDGF-BB in orofacial bone regeneration: systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs
evidence.finding: Pooled RCTs show rhBMP-2 and rhPDGF-BB produce orofacial bone gains comparable to conventional grafts without a clear advantage, with dose and indication effects unresolved.

evidence.title: Evaluation of maxillary alveolar reconstruction using a resorbable collagen sponge with rhBMP-2 in cleft lip and palate patients
evidence.finding: Children 8 to 12: rhBMP-2 group reached 65 percent mean bone height at 12 months versus 83.8 percent at 6 months with iliac crest; significant swelling in 37.5 percent of the rhBMP-2 arm versus donor-site pain in 87.5 percent of the ICBG arm.

evidence.title: Human bone morphogenetic protein-2 use for maxillary reconstruction in cleft lip and palate patients
evidence.finding: Formed bone volume, formation rate, height repair and density were similar for rhBMP-2 and iliac crest at one year; periosteoplasty arm abandoned for insufficient bone.

evidence.title: Efficacy of rhBMP-2 in alveolar cleft treatment for children: systematic review and meta-analysis
evidence.finding: Six RCTs and two non-randomized studies: bone volume 61.1 percent with rhBMP-2 versus 59.1 percent with iliac crest, bone height lower with rhBMP-2 (about 61 versus 79 percent), moderate-quality evidence of no significant difference.

evidence.title: Effectiveness of rhBMP-2 versus iliac autogenous bone graft in cleft patients: umbrella review
evidence.finding: Six systematic reviews, bone fill 74.2 percent rhBMP-2 versus 72.4 percent autogenous, none at low risk of bias; recommends caution in children.

evidence.title: rhBMP-2 as an alternative to autologous bone graft in pediatric craniofacial reconstruction: systematic review
evidence.finding: 21 studies (6 RCTs): in alveolar cleft 4 of 12 favored rhBMP-2 for bone formation, 1 favored ICBG, 7 no difference; facial edema the commonest rhBMP-2 complication; all five operative-time studies favored rhBMP-2.

evidence.title: Reconstruction of mandibular continuity defects with rhBMP-2
evidence.finding: 14 body and angle defects from tumor or osteomyelitis regenerated with rhBMP-2 on collagen alone under tenting hardware; all restored to prosthetic function at 6 to 18 months.

evidence.title: Off-label use of rhBMP-2 for reconstruction of mandibular bone defects in humans
evidence.finding: Three of five defects healed; both failures were continuity defects, salvaged with iliac crest.

evidence.title: Safety and efficacy of rhBMP-2 in craniofacial surgery
evidence.finding: 17 RCTs (n 7 to 160) support use in sinus and alveolar settings; evidence fails to support rhBMP-2 for maxillary sinus wall augmentation, calvarial reconstruction, mandibular reconstruction or distraction osteogenesis.

evidence.title: Cost effectiveness in alveolar bone grafting in patients with cleft lip and palate: randomized clinical trial (DBM/BMP vs ICBG)
evidence.finding: Recruiting at UT Health Houston, ages 6 to 15, primary endpoint health-system cost per successful graft at one year; completion 2028.

bd.reimbursement: Inpatient: bundled in the level-based spinal fusion MS-DRG family in force since FY2025 (402, 426-430, 447-451, 456-458; 523-525 added FY2027; 471-473 cervical) and 471-473 (cervical); no separate HCPCS; physician add-on +20930 (osteopromotive material) is a bundled 0-RVU code for Medicare. Payer medical policies commonly cover rhBMP-2 only for on-label lumbar interbody use and deny cervical use.
bd.notes: Priced at several thousand dollars per kit (ISSG mean $14,000 per deformity case); Medtronic's TLIF label (Feb 2026) and Breakthrough designation (Apr 2024) are the first new spine indications since 2018. Kuros MagnetOs is now sold by the Medtronic spine sales force under a 2025 agency agreement, giving Medtronic a non-BMP alternative in the same bag.
bd.challenge: C9359 attribution and current OPPS packaging status for Infuse not re-verified in this sweep.

challenge: FDA's July 1, 2008 Public Health Notification (CDRH, signed Daniel G. Schultz) was retrieved via the Wayback Machine: at least 38 reports over four years of neck/throat swelling with airway compression after cervical rhBMP use, most at 2-14 days; FDA states safety and effectiveness in the cervical spine 'have not been demonstrated' and recommends approved alternatives or enrollment in approved studies. The TLIF supplement is P000058/S096 (panel track, decision 02/13/2026). Remaining gap: Medtronic's release gives only 'fusion rates exceeding 90 percent in single-level TLIF' for Infuse (493 randomized 1:1:1 to 2.1 mg/level, 4.2 mg/level, local autograft; stopped for success at the first interim analysis of 480 treated patients); the autograft-arm and two-level percentages are unpublished.

name: Augment Bone Graft
ownership_history: Developed by BioMimetic Therapeutics (Franklin, TN); BioMimetic acquired by Wright Medical Group 2013; Wright Medical acquired by Stryker (closed November 2020). Stryker still lists Augment Bone Graft and Augment Injectable in its Trauma & Extremities biologics line as of this review; no divestiture found.
composition: Recombinant human platelet-derived growth factor-BB (0.3 mg/mL, yeast-expressed) with beta-tricalcium phosphate granules; drug-device combination product

on_label_indications: As an alternative to autograft in arthrodesis (surgical fusion) of the ankle and/or hindfoot joints in patients with osteoarthritis, post-traumatic, rheumatoid or psoriatic arthritis, avascular necrosis, joint instability or deformity, congenital defects, or other joint arthropathies, who need supplemental graft material on pre- or intraoperative assessment (summary of the approval order; FDA PMA P100006, decision 2015-09-01)

applications.evidence_summary: DiGiovanni 2013 (JBJS; PMID 23824386): 434 patients at 37 North American sites randomized 2:1 to rhPDGF-BB/beta-TCP or autograft for hindfoot or ankle fusion; CT fusion at 6 months 61.2% of patients (66.5% of joints) vs 62.0% (62.6%), clinical healing at 52 weeks 86.2% vs 87.6%, noninferior with less pain and fewer graft-site complications.
applications.caveats: Sponsor-funded (BioMimetic); noninferiority design against autograft; absolute 6-month CT fusion rates in the low 60s on both arms; two-thirds of enrolled joints were hindfoot rather than tibiotalar.

applications.evidence_summary: Same pivotal RCT (PMID 23824386); subtalar, talonavicular and calcaneocuboid joints made up most of the 597 joints analyzed.
applications.caveats: Sponsor-funded; no subgroup powered for any single joint.

applications.evidence_summary: Label is for primary arthrodesis; no revision or nonunion trial found.
applications.caveats: Off-label in revision; CMS cited a post-hoc finding that patients 65 and older were more than twice as likely to fuse with Augment than autograft, which has not been prospectively replicated.

evidence.title: Recombinant human platelet-derived growth factor-BB and beta-tricalcium phosphate (rhPDGF-BB/beta-TCP): an alternative to autogenous bone graft
evidence.finding: Noninferior to autograft for hindfoot/ankle fusion on CT at 6 months and clinical healing at 52 weeks, with less pain and fewer side effects.

evidence.title: Prospective, randomized, multi-center feasibility trial of rhPDGF-BB versus autologous bone graft in a foot and ankle fusion model
evidence.finding: Radiographic union 77% Augment vs 50% autograft at 36 weeks in a 20-patient pilot; surgery 26 minutes shorter without harvest.

evidence.title: Pivotal trial of Augment Bone Graft vs autologous bone graft in foot and ankle fusions
evidence.finding: Registry entry for the pivotal trial (enrollment 414 listed; 434 in the publication); completed, primary completion January 2010.

evidence.title: Post-approval trial of Augment Bone Graft vs autologous bone graft in foot and ankle fusions
evidence.finding: FDA-required post-approval study; status listed as unknown on ClinicalTrials.gov, no results posted.

bd.reimbursement: Inpatient: bundled in the MS-DRG. Hospital outpatient and ASC: CMS granted transitional pass-through status under device category C1734 effective 2020-01-01, billed with ankle/hindfoot arthrodesis CPT codes (27870 and related), after finding substantial clinical improvement from eliminating donor-site pain; pass-through lasts two to three years, so the product is now packaged into the procedure APC/ASC rate (exact expiry date not verified in this sweep).
bd.notes: Carried by Stryker Foot & Ankle (ex-Wright) reps alongside Prophecy/Infinity ankle and hindfoot nail systems; the only PMA-approved osteoinductive product with a foot-and-ankle label, which is its core contracting argument against 361 cellular allografts. The pass-through window (2020-2022/23) was the main commercial catalyst after approval.

catalog_status_2026: Stryker's US trauma-and-extremities bone grafting catalog page (read 2026-10-22) lists AlloFiber, AlloMatrix, Augment, BIO4, DBM, FusionFlex, HydroSet XT, Ignite, OsteoSet, Pro-Dense, Pro-Dense LoVisc, Pro-Stim, Tensix, Vitoss, Vitoss BA, Vitoss BA2X and Vitoss BBTrauma as current products.

name: Augment Injectable Bone Graft
ownership_history: Same chain as Augment Bone Graft: BioMimetic Therapeutics to Wright Medical (2013) to Stryker (2020).
composition: rhPDGF-BB (0.3 mg/mL) with an injectable beta-tricalcium phosphate and bovine type I collagen matrix

on_label_indications: Same indication as Augment Bone Graft: alternative to autograft in ankle and hindfoot arthrodesis (PMA supplement S005, approval notice dated 2018-06-12)

applications.evidence_summary: Daniels 2015 (FAI; PMID 25848134): 75 patients randomized 5:1 (63 Augment Injectable, 12 autograft) plus 142 autograft controls from the parallel Augment trial; complete CT fusion at 24 weeks 84% vs 65% (p<0.001), clinical success at 52 weeks 91% vs 78%.
applications.caveats: Sponsor-funded (Wright Medical author); only 12 concurrent randomized controls, the rest borrowed from a separate trial with an identical protocol; superiority signal rests on that pooled control.

applications.evidence_summary: Same trial (PMID 25848134); NCT01305356 lists 299 enrolled.
applications.caveats: As above.

evidence.title: Prospective randomized controlled trial of hindfoot and ankle fusions treated with rhPDGF-BB in combination with a beta-TCP-collagen matrix
evidence.finding: 24-week CT fusion 84% vs 65% autograft; mean time to fusion 14.3 vs 19.7 weeks; two harvest-site infections in controls.

evidence.title: Pivotal trial of Augment Injectable Bone Graft vs autologous bone graft in hindfoot fusions
evidence.finding: Completed April 2013 at 25 sites; supported the 2018 PMA supplement.

evidence.title: Post-approval trial of Augment Injectable vs autologous bone graft in foot and ankle fusions
evidence.finding: Post-approval study; status unknown, no results posted.

bd.reimbursement: Covered by the same C1734 pass-through category as Augment Bone Graft from 2020-01-01 in HOPD and ASC; now packaged. Inpatient bundled in MS-DRG.
bd.notes: Injectable form was built for percutaneous and arthroscopic fusions and ASC workflow; 1.5 cc and 3.0 cc kits.

catalog_status_2026: Stryker's US trauma-and-extremities bone grafting catalog page (read 2026-10-22) lists AlloFiber, AlloMatrix, Augment, BIO4, DBM, FusionFlex, HydroSet XT, Ignite, OsteoSet, Pro-Dense, Pro-Dense LoVisc, Pro-Stim, Tensix, Vitoss, Vitoss BA, Vitoss BA2X and Vitoss BBTrauma as current products.

name: GEM 21S Growth-factor Enhanced Matrix (rhPDGF-BB with beta-TCP)
ownership_history: Developed by BioMimetic Pharmaceuticals (Samuel Lynch); PMA held by Lynch Biologics, LLC since approval; the orthopedic sibling Augment (rhPDGF-BB) went BioMimetic to Wright Medical (2013) to Stryker (2020). GEM 21S was marketed in dentistry by Osteohealth (a Luitpold Pharmaceuticals unit, which also packaged the kit) and Luitpold's Shirley, NY plant manufactured the rhPDGF syringe; current distributor not verified.
composition: 0.3 mg/mL recombinant human PDGF-BB (0.5 mL syringe) mixed chairside with 0.5 cc beta-tricalcium phosphate particles

regulatory.reference: P040013 approved 2005-11-18; supplements through S032 (2024-11-22)
on_label_indications: Treatment of periodontally related defects: intrabony periodontal defects, furcation periodontal defects, and gingival recession associated with periodontal defects

applications.evidence_summary: Pivotal 11-center RCT (Nevins 2005, n=180, intrabony defects of 4 mm or more): rhPDGF-BB with beta-TCP accelerated clinical attachment gain and increased linear bone fill at six months versus beta-TCP alone.
applications.caveats: Sponsor-run; six-month surrogate endpoints; a 2019 meta-analysis found rhPDGF gains comparable to conventional grafting.

applications.evidence_summary: Off-label in sinus lifts and ridge augmentation; the 2013 systematic review found no evidence to support rhPDGF in sinus lift, socket healing or ridge augmentation.
applications.caveats: Off-label.

applications.evidence_summary: Three-patient pilot of cultured marrow MSCs on biphasic scaffold with PDGF in alveolar clefts gave 51 percent fill at three months (2011).
applications.caveats: Off-label, cell-plus-growth-factor construct.

evidence.title: Platelet-derived growth factor stimulates bone fill and rate of attachment level gain: results of a large multicenter randomized controlled trial
evidence.finding: rhPDGF-BB with beta-TCP produced faster clinical attachment gain and more linear bone fill at six months than beta-TCP alone in advanced intrabony defects.

evidence.title: Clinical efficacy of growth factors to enhance tissue repair in oral and maxillofacial reconstruction: systematic review
evidence.finding: rhPDGF-BB reliably increases linear bone fill in intrabony pockets with weaker evidence for lasting attachment gains; no evidence for recession, sinus lift, socket or ridge augmentation; rhBMP-2 effective in sockets and sinus lifts; no controlled data for mandibular segmental repair.

evidence.title: Repair of alveolar cleft defect with mesenchymal stem cells and platelet derived growth factors: preliminary report
evidence.finding: Mean 51.3 percent defect fill at three months in four alveolar clefts treated with cultured marrow MSCs on biphasic scaffold plus rhPDGF.

bd.reimbursement: Periodontal regeneration is CDT D4263 and D4265; private pay or dental plan; no medical code.
bd.notes: The only rhPDGF product in dentistry; low visibility, no new indication since 2005; post-approval study protocols approved 2008 and 2015.

name: Acellular human dermal allograft patches for rotator cuff augmentation (GraftJacket, ArthroFlex, others)
company: GraftJacket: LifeCell/Allergan-processed, marketed by Wright Medical, now Stryker (orthopaedic rights; unverified); ArthroFlex: LifeNet Health, distributed by Arthrex
ownership_history: GraftJacket (Wright Medical, 2002 onward) moved to Stryker with the 2020 Wright acquisition; ArthroFlex launched by Arthrex/LifeNet around 2011 (dates from memory, unverified).
composition: Decellularized human dermis, 1-2 mm thick, sutured over or bridging the repaired cuff; regulated as a 361 HCT/P (no openFDA 510(k) record found for either brand).

regulatory.reference: No premarket number
on_label_indications: none; 361 tissue used at surgeon discretion for tendon augmentation or superior capsular reconstruction

applications.evidence_summary: Multicenter RCT of 42 patients with 2-tendon tears >3 cm: GraftJacket augmentation improved ASES (98.9 vs 94.8) and Constant (91.9 vs 85.3) scores at 24 months with better MRI intact-repair rates (Barber 2012, PMID:21978432). Arthrex is running a 120-patient randomized post-market study of dermal allograft augmentation in large/massive tears (NCT05981833, 2023-2025, status unknown).
applications.caveats: Single small RCT, industry-supported; most other data are superior capsular reconstruction series rather than augmentation.

evidence.title: A prospective, randomized evaluation of acellular human dermal matrix augmentation for arthroscopic rotator cuff repair
evidence.finding: Statistically better ASES and Constant scores with augmentation at mean 24 months.

evidence.title: Randomized post-market study evaluating dermal allograft augmentation of large and massive rotator cuff tears
evidence.finding: Arthrex-sponsored; primary completion September 2025; status unknown.

bd.reimbursement: Packaged into the ASC/HOPD procedure payment; in HOPD the tissue may be reported with HCPCS C1762 (connective tissue, human) but it is packaged, not separately paid.
bd.notes: Tissue-bank margin flows to the distributor (Arthrex, Stryker); the same reps sell anchors and the bone biologics in the atlas.

challenge: Tried Stryker's US GraftJacket and trauma-and-extremities pages (404) and openFDA (no GraftJacket 510(k) under the GRAFTJACKET or LIFECELL names); no primary source stating the regulatory status or the current Stryker/LifeCell/Allergan rights was retrieved. 361 status is the working assumption.

name: CornerLoc SI Joint Fusion grafts
composition: Two machined cortical bone allografts placed orthogonally into the prepared posterior joint through two small incisions, with a demineralized bone matrix sponge; non-transfixing. The company's TransLoc 3D (K232878, Oct 2023) is a 3D-printed titanium modular posterior implant plus lateral-oblique screws (hybrid) and is a device.

on_label_indications: Homologous use: structural allograft bone placed in the sacroiliac joint (HCT/P, no FDA-cleared indication)

applications.evidence_summary: No peer-reviewed clinical series of the allograft retrieved; physician and hospital pages (UK HealthCare) describe the technique and a 12-month ossification timeline. CornerLoc's registered studies (NCT05916092 SPARTAN n=240; NCT06487936 registry) cover the titanium TransLoc 3D.
applications.caveats: Company founded 2017 (Tulsa, OK); evidence for the graft product is descriptive only; the hybrid TransLoc 3D exists because the posterior allograft alone is non-covered under the 2025 LCDs.

evidence.title: SPARTAN: post-market study of TransLoc 3D screw-only vs hybrid constructs
evidence.finding: Company reports 91.7% improved in pain and function at 6 months (interim, unpublished).

bd.reimbursement: CPT 27278 (intra-articular, no cortical piercing) unless a cortical-piercing variant or hybrid (27279); ASC device-intensive 2026; non-covered by CGS/Noridian/Palmetto LCDs (transfixation required); implant packaged, no separate HCPCS.
bd.notes: Private; sells surgery-ready trays to pain practices and ASCs. The DBM sponge is unbranded in all sources.

challenge: Tissue bank and the DBM brand are not disclosed; launch year inferred from the 2017 founding and 2018-2019 physician adoption, not a dated release.

name: Cortical strut / fibular strut allograft (structural allograft)
company: Tissue banks (MTF Biologics, AlloSource, LifeNet Health, RTI/Surgalign heritage) and distributing implant companies
composition: Freeze-dried or fresh-frozen human cortical bone (fibular shaft segments, femoral or tibial cortical struts), sometimes machined; minimally manipulated, homologous use.

regulatory.reference: Regulated solely under section 361 of the PHS Act and 21 CFR 1271 (establishment registration, no premarket review)
on_label_indications: Not labeled with indications; HCT/P for homologous structural use as determined by the surgeon

applications.evidence_summary: Haddad/Duncan 2002 multicenter series: 39 of 40 Vancouver B1 fractures united with cortical onlay strut allografts alone (19) or with a plate (21), with increased bone stock. A later pooled review of locking-plate fixation (135 fractures, 91% union) and a 20-patient series without struts (18 of 19 healed) show modern plates reduce but do not eliminate the role of struts, which are reserved for poor bone stock and medial comminution.
applications.caveats: Retrospective; allograft resorption and stress shielding over the long term not addressed.

applications.evidence_summary: Non-vascularized fibular (auto- or allo-) graft across the neck with revision fixation is reported in small series, mostly from India and China; vascularized fibular autograft series report union in all patients (n=13, n=29).
applications.caveats: Small series; the US standard for young patients is valgus osteotomy.

applications.evidence_summary: Free vascularized fibular autograft (Urbaniak) is the structural benchmark for pre-collapse lesions; non-vascularized fibular allograft is a lower-morbidity alternative. A 2023 network meta-analysis of 18 RCTs ranked free fibula and vascularized bone grafting above core decompression alone for preventing progression.
applications.caveats: Autograft, not allograft, in most RCTs; technically demanding.

applications.evidence_summary: Best-supported augmentation in upper-extremity trauma: meta-analysis of 10 studies (n=802) found fibular allograft with a locking plate preserved humeral head height (WMD -2.40 mm) and neck-shaft angle (WMD -5.71 degrees), improved ASES (+5.08) and cut major complications (OR 0.37) with no difference in revision (Dasari 2022, PMID:34906682). A 2026 meta-analysis restricted to 5 RCTs (n=350) found graft augmentation lowered complications (OR 0.21) and biologic grafts shortened healing by 3.25 weeks (Daher 2026, PMID:42750779). Cadaver loading: 0 of 8 augmented vs 6 of 8 unaugmented constructs collapsed (PMID:21782474).
applications.caveats: Mostly retrospective comparisons and Chinese single-center RCTs; graft fate (incorporation vs resorption) and long-term outcomes undefined (PMID:32030961); a new RCT uses femoral head allograft instead (NCT07538700, 2025-2029). No proof that augmentation beats reverse arthroplasty in the 75+ group where ORIF volume is falling.

evidence.title: Periprosthetic femoral fractures around well-fixed implants: use of cortical onlay allografts with or without a plate.
evidence.finding: 98% union with strut allografts with or without a plate; struts act as biological plates and add bone stock.

evidence.title: Comparative analysis of surgical interventions for osteonecrosis of the femoral head: a network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
evidence.finding: Across 18 RCTs, autologous bone grafting plus BMAC, free fibula, vascularized bone graft and biomaterial plus vascularized graft all delayed progression versus core decompression alone; no difference in THA conversion.

evidence.title: Free vascularised fibular graft for neglected femoral neck fractures in young adults.
evidence.finding: All 13 neglected femoral neck fractures united at a mean 4.8 months; coxa vara common.

evidence.title: Improved outcomes for proximal humerus fracture ORIF augmented with a fibular allograft in elderly patients: systematic review and meta-analysis
evidence.finding: Better radiographic maintenance, ASES and fewer major complications with fibular allograft; no revision difference.

evidence.title: Bone graft augmentation reduces complications in osteosynthesis of proximal humerus fractures: meta-analysis of RCTs
evidence.finding: Five RCTs; OR 0.21 for complications; biologic grafts healed 3.25 weeks faster with less pain.

evidence.title: Indirect medial reduction and strut support of proximal humerus fractures using an endosteal implant
evidence.finding: Technique description of the endosteal fibular allograft incorporated into the locking construct.

evidence.title: Proximal humeral fracture fixation: locking plate construct with or without intramedullary fibular allograft
evidence.finding: No augmented construct collapsed under 25,000 cycles vs 6 of 8 unaugmented.

evidence.title: Hip-allograft in proximal humerus fractures versus plate implantation alone: RCT
evidence.finding: Recruiting (Netherlands); femoral head allograft vs plate alone; primary completion May 2029.

bd.reimbursement: Bundled in inpatient MS-DRG (revision THA or periprosthetic fracture DRGs); allograft cost is a hospital supply expense.
bd.notes: Commodity-priced, tissue-bank supplied, usually contracted through the hospital's tissue services agreement rather than the implant contract; implant companies co-market struts with cable-plate systems.

ownership_history: Not a branded product; cortical fibula segments are standard tissue-bank inventory. The endosteal technique was described by Gardner, Helfet and Lorich at HSS (Gardner 2008, PMID:18317054).

name: Fresh distal tibia allograft (DTA) for glenoid reconstruction
company: Tissue banks supplying fresh osteochondral grafts (JRF Ortho, MTF Biologics); technique popularized by Provencher
ownership_history: Not branded; fresh (non-frozen) lateral distal tibia plafond segments are allocated by tissue banks with a short shelf life.
composition: Fresh osteochondral lateral distal tibia, cut to match the anterior glenoid defect and fixed with two screws or suture buttons.

regulatory.reference: No premarket number; fresh osteochondral allograft under 21 CFR 1271
on_label_indications: none

applications.evidence_summary: Matched cohort of 50 DTA vs 50 Latarjet with at least 15% bone loss: equivalent ASES, WOSI and SANE at 45 months despite larger defects in the DTA group (Frank 2018, PMID:29389219). DTA case series: 89% graft healing on CT, 3% lysis, no recurrence in 27 patients (Provencher 2017, PMID:28017469). Systematic review of allograft glenoid reconstruction (283 shoulders): recurrence 3.9%, healing 93.5% (Villatte 2020, PMID:32524228). First RCT vs Latarjet recruiting (NCT05658289, n=68).
applications.caveats: Retrospective and single-surgeon data; fresh graft logistics and cost; resorption concerns after arthroscopic DTA (Wong 2018, PMID:30095986).

evidence.title: Outcomes of Latarjet versus distal tibia allograft for anterior shoulder instability repair: a matched cohort analysis
evidence.finding: No significant difference in postoperative scores between Latarjet and DTA.

evidence.title: Distal tibia allograft glenoid reconstruction in recurrent anterior shoulder instability: clinical and radiographic outcomes
evidence.finding: ASES 63 to 91; 89% allograft healing; no recurrent instability at 45 months.

evidence.title: Use of allograft to reconstruct anterior bony glenoid defect in chronic glenohumeral instability: a systematic review
evidence.finding: Recurrence 3.9%, allograft healing 93.5% across 10 studies.

evidence.title: Latarjet vs anatomic glenoid reconstruction (DTA with Bankart repair): prospective multicentre RCT
evidence.finding: Recruiting; primary completion January 2026.

bd.reimbursement: Shoulder stabilization with bone block is an outpatient/ASC procedure; the fresh graft is packaged into the facility payment (in HOPD it may be reported with the connective-tissue HCPCS C1762 but is still packaged). The graft's price (thousands of dollars) is the commercial obstacle vs a free coracoid.
bd.notes: Sports-medicine reps (Arthrex, Smith+Nephew, Stryker, DePuy Mitek) sell the fixation and the instruments; the tissue bank sells the graft. A BD role here is about tissue-bank partnerships, not a device.

name: LinQ SI Joint Stabilization System (and TRAQ)
composition: Machined structural cortical bone allograft ('almond-shaped' with a graft window), placed posteriorly into the decorticated mid-joint; TRAQ (2026) is a cortical-piercing allograft variant engaging sacral and iliac cortices at four points. Window may be packed with DBM at surgeon discretion (physician descriptions; not in the IFU text retrieved).
