on_label_indications: Homologous use: structural allograft bone placed in the sacroiliac joint (HCT/P, no FDA-cleared indication)

applications.evidence_summary: SECURE (NCT04423120; Calodney 2024, PMID 38524688): prospective single-arm, 16 US sites, 122 implanted, composite responder 73.5% at 12 months, one procedure-related SAE; no CT fusion endpoint. Bovinet 2025 (PMID 40832586): retrospective 6-site cohort n=258, NRS 7.6 to 1.6 at mean 1.75 years. Ampomah 2025 (PMID 40828365): n=260, AE 1.9% at 6 months. LINQT RCT vs conservative management (NCT07558278, n=200, started Jul 2026) is the first randomized trial of any posterior allograft.
applications.caveats: All clinical data are pain/function case series by interventional pain physicians with company involvement; no radiographic fusion rate; no comparison to lateral transfixing implants; three MAC LCDs (2025) non-cover procedures without a transfixation device.

evidence.title: SECURE: single-arm multicenter prospective study of LinQ
evidence.finding: 73.5% composite responders at 12 months; one procedure-related serious AE.

evidence.title: Safety, efficacy and durability of outcomes: results from SECURE
evidence.finding: VAS and ODI significantly improved at 12 months; responder rate stable 66-74% across visits.

evidence.title: Minimally invasive posterior SI joint fusion with a novel cortical allograft: real-world long-term outcomes, multisite US cohort
evidence.finding: Mean NRS reduction 6.0 points at 91 weeks; no serious AEs reported.

evidence.title: Retrospective evaluation of adverse events in posterior approach with bone allograft
evidence.finding: AE incidence 2.3% at 3 months and 1.9% at 6 months; no device-related events.

evidence.title: Multicenter retrospective analysis of a posterior sacroiliac fusion device (LinQ)
evidence.finding: NRS 6.98 to 3.06 at mean 612 days; no major AEs.

evidence.title: LINQT: open-label RCT of LinQ vs conventional medical management
evidence.finding: Enrolling; primary endpoint composite responder at 6 months, follow-up 24 months.

evidence.title: TRAQTION: post-market single-arm study of TRAQ
evidence.finding: Enrolling; 24-month follow-up.

bd.reimbursement: CPT 27278 (intra-articular, no cortical piercing) unless a cortical-piercing variant or hybrid (27279); ASC device-intensive 2026; non-covered by CGS/Noridian/Palmetto LCDs (transfixation required); implant packaged, no separate HCPCS.
bd.notes: PainTEQ's clinician page states LinQ and TRAQ are HCT/Ps 'regulated solely under Section 361' and 'not FDA-cleared or FDA-approved medical devices'. PainTEQ drove the 0775T (2022) and 27278 (2024) code applications using SECURE interim data. Company ranked on Inc. 5000 (2024). Office-based-lab 27278 physician payment ($13,834 in 2026) is the economic engine for interventional pain practices.

ownership_history: PainTEQ (Tampa, FL) private; majority growth recapitalization co-led by Signet Healthcare Partners and Windham Capital Partners, Aug 2025.
challenge: Tissue bank that processes LinQ not disclosed in any public source retrieved; 'DBM packed in the window' comes from physician/trade descriptions, not the IFU.

name: PsiF Posterior SI Fusion allograft
composition: Structural allograft bone implant placed through a postero-inferior intra-articular trajectory into a decorticated channel in the articular joint, secured mortise-and-tenon in subchondral bone (Lynch 2022). PsiF DNA (510(k) May 2025, launched Jan 2026) is a titanium double-helix transfixing implant placed ilium-to-sacrum that is packed with graft and leverages self-harvested autograft; PsiFGuard (SpineGuard, K-cleared Oct 2024) is the drilling-guidance device.

on_label_indications: Homologous use: structural allograft bone placed in the sacroiliac joint (HCT/P, no FDA-cleared indication)

applications.evidence_summary: Lynch 2022 (PMID 36420375): 57-patient multicenter registry, back pain 6.8 to 3.8 at 6 months. Kaye 2024 (PMID 39087970): LSU Shreveport single-center series of 72 posterior fusions (83% LinQ, remainder PsiF), VAS -3.6 cm, no procedure-related AEs, 54% with one-year follow-up. Latif 2023 (PMID 37511749) is a technique paper for PsiF DNA.
applications.caveats: Small registries with company-affiliated authors; PsiF results are pooled with LinQ in the only independent series; no fusion imaging endpoint.

evidence.title: Minimally invasive inferior intra-articular SI joint fusion with allograft bone
evidence.finding: Back pain 6.8 to 3.8 at 6 months; all outcomes p<0.001; no fusion endpoint.

evidence.title: Posterior sacroiliac fusion surgery: retrospective single-center study (LinQ and PsiF)
evidence.finding: VAS -3.6 cm from 9.5; 38.5% with >=50% improvement; zero procedure-related AEs; 26% withdrawal.

bd.reimbursement: CPT 27278 (intra-articular, no cortical piercing) unless a cortical-piercing variant or hybrid (27279); ASC device-intensive 2026; non-covered by CGS/Noridian/Palmetto LCDs (transfixation required); implant packaged, no separate HCPCS.
bd.notes: Omnia Medical (Morgantown, WV), private. The shift from the PsiF allograft to the 510(k) titanium PsiF DNA (transfixing, 27279-eligible) is the clearest example of a posterior vendor re-engineering around the 2025 LCDs.

challenge: Omnia's site does not describe the original PsiF implant's material; its allograft nature is taken from Kaye 2024 ('sacroiliac fusion allograft implants ... PsiF System from Omnia Medical') and Lynch 2022. Tissue bank and launch year not disclosed.

name: SiLO Posterior SI-Fusion System (allograft)
composition: Single dowel of human cortical bone with three circumferential ridges ('Dowel Anchorage Design') and dual vertical side channels that accept additional bone graft during insertion; posterior intra-articular, non-transfixing. SiLO TFX (K221047, Oct 2022; titanium cone plus ilium and sacrum screws, graft placed in the barrel) is the company's 510(k) transfixing hybrid and is a device, not a biologic.

on_label_indications: Homologous use: structural allograft bone placed in the sacroiliac joint (HCT/P, no FDA-cleared indication)

applications.evidence_summary: No peer-reviewed clinical series for the SiLO allograft was retrieved; the company reported >2,500 SiLO procedures in the US (June 2025 release) and a cadaveric study of SiLO TFX. Aurora launched 'Aurora Biologics' in late 2025 to sell biologics with its implants.
applications.caveats: Company-reported volume only; SiLO TFX revenue grew 135% in 2024 and aggregate SI implant sales +8.4% in 2025 (press releases), implying the titanium hybrid, not the allograft, is the growth product after the 2025 LCDs.

bd.reimbursement: CPT 27278 (intra-articular, no cortical piercing) unless a cortical-piercing variant or hybrid (27279); ASC device-intensive 2026; non-covered by CGS/Noridian/Palmetto LCDs (transfixation required); implant packaged, no separate HCPCS.
bd.notes: Aurora Spine (TSXV: ASG / OTC: ASAPF), FY2025 revenue $18.4M (+4.6%); SI implants are one of three product lines. Distributor-based sales.

challenge: Tissue processor not disclosed; no clinical outcomes paper found for the allograft; SiLO vs SiLO TFX volumes not separated.

name: Structural allograft (femoral head, bulk tricortical and shaped allograft wedges)
company: Tissue banks (MTF Biologics, AlloSource, LifeNet Health, RTI/Surgalign successors) and hardware companies that private-label allograft wedges
ownership_history: Not applicable.
composition: Fresh-frozen or freeze-dried human femoral head or cortical-cancellous block, shaped intraoperatively or supplied as preformed wedges (Cotton, Evans, interposition)

regulatory.reference: none
on_label_indications: Homologous use as structural bone graft; no FDA-reviewed indication

applications.evidence_summary: Cifaldi 2022 (PMID 35585002): systematic review of 11 studies, 175 patients with TTC arthrodesis and structural allograft (mostly femoral head with a retrograde nail); union 67.4%, limb salvage 92.5%, complications 26.6%, allograft collapse 1.2%. Jeng 2013 (PMID 23650649): 32 patients, 50% radiographic fusion, every diabetic patient a nonunion, 19% below-knee amputation, 71% functional limb salvage counting asymptomatic nonunions.
applications.caveats: High nonunion despite high limb salvage; 3D-printed titanium cages now report 88-89% pooled union (PMID 41724588, PMID 42600975) and one comparative study favored the cage over femoral head for fusion and subsidence.

applications.evidence_summary: Femoral-head and bulk allograft used to restore medial-column length after wedge resection; PMID 34677103 reported high fusion in 14 bone-block TTC fusions with allograft plus BMAC plus DBM and prolonged protected weight-bearing.
applications.caveats: Small series; Charcot subgroup outcomes worse.

applications.evidence_summary: Interposition allograft block for salvage of failed first MTP implant arthroplasty; pooled nonunion 16.5% across 76 patients (PMID 37165627).
applications.caveats: Six level-IV studies.

applications.evidence_summary: Preformed allograft wedges are the most common Cotton and Evans osteotomy spacer; no comparative outcome data found.
applications.caveats: Expert practice.

evidence.title: Tibiotalocalcaneal arthrodesis with structural allograft for management of large osseous defects of the hindfoot and ankle: a systematic review and meta-analysis
evidence.finding: Union 67.4%, limb salvage 92.5%; no difference nail vs plate.

evidence.title: Tibiotalocalcaneal arthrodesis with bulk femoral head allograft for salvage of large defects in the ankle
evidence.finding: 50% fusion; diabetes the only predictor of nonunion; 19% amputation.

evidence.title: Tibiotalocalcaneal arthrodesis using a novel retrograde intramedullary nail
evidence.finding: 70% fusion overall; 76.5% in the 17 patients needing femoral-head allograft.

evidence.title: Patient-specific 3D-printed porous titanium implants for complex foot and ankle reconstruction: a current concepts review
evidence.finding: Pooled union 89%, limb salvage 92%, reoperation 26%; the single comparative study favored the cage over femoral-head allograft.

bd.reimbursement: No separate payment; bundled or packaged. Allograft is usually procured under the hospital's tissue-bank agreement.
bd.notes: Commodity-priced; the competitive threat is custom 3D-printed titanium (restor3d, 4WEB, Paragon 28/Zimmer Biomet) which carries a much higher ASP and is displacing femoral head in TTC salvage at academic centers.

name: Structural cortical allograft rings and blocks for ACDF (e.g., Cornerstone-SR, AVS/ Bio AVS, MTF and AlloSource cortical rings)
company: Multiple (MTF Biologics, AlloSource, LifeNet Health, RTI/Xtant; branded by Medtronic, Stryker, DePuy Synthes, Globus and others)
ownership_history: Commodity tissue-bank product supplied under private label to most spine companies; Medtronic's Cornerstone-SR ring was the carrier in its cervical rhBMP-2 trials.
composition: Machined cortical (fibula or femoral ring) or corticocancellous allograft spacers with a central window for graft; often paired with a filler (local bone, DBM, i-FACTOR, cellular allograft)

regulatory.reference: Section 361 HCT/P (minimally manipulated structural bone)
on_label_indications: Structural bone graft for cervical interbody fusion (homologous use); PEEK and titanium spacers are devices, not biologics

applications.evidence_summary: Meta-analysis of prospective plated ACDF studies: pseudarthrosis 4.8% with allograft vs 0.9% with autograft (Shriver 2015); 2024 meta-analysis of 34 studies/3,451 segments found structural allograft fusion rates not different from cages at 3-12 months but more hardware complications (Li 2024).
applications.caveats: Comparisons are across studies, not head-to-head RCTs; dysphagia rates do not differ between allograft and autograft (Shriver 2017).

evidence.title: Pseudoarthrosis rates in anterior cervical discectomy and fusion: a meta-analysis
evidence.finding: Overall pseudarthrosis 2.6%; autograft 0.9% vs allograft 4.8%.

evidence.title: Fusion rates at different times of cortical iliac crest autograft or allograft compared with cages after ACDF: a meta-analysis
evidence.finding: Structural allograft vs cage: no significant fusion difference at 3, 6 or 12 months; higher hardware complications with allograft.

bd.reimbursement: Inpatient bundled in MS-DRGs 471-473; physician add-on +20931 (structural allograft) is separately reportable and, unlike +20930, is not a Medicare 0-RVU bundled code (confirm current status indicator).
bd.notes: Low-margin commodity; the strategic value is in the filler sold with the ring (i-FACTOR, cellular allografts). MTF, AlloSource and LifeNet all private-label rings for device companies.

name: Vyrsa Pro cortical allograft (Vyrsa V1 titanium is the device)
company: Globus Medical (via Nevro, via Vyrsa Technologies)
composition: Custom cortical allograft implant for posterior SI joint fusion delivered through an 'inferior inlet' approach (Nevro acquisition release, Nov 2023). Vyrsa V1 (introduced end-2022) and Nevro1 (NCT06909292, 'SI transfixing and fusion system') are the titanium transfixing systems in the same portfolio.

on_label_indications: Homologous use: structural allograft bone placed in the sacroiliac joint (HCT/P, no FDA-cleared indication)

applications.evidence_summary: No clinical publication retrieved for Vyrsa Pro. Nevro's post-market study NCT06909292 (n=180, completed May 2025) covers the titanium Nevro1 transfixing system.
applications.caveats: Portfolio changed hands twice in 17 months (Vyrsa -> Nevro, 30 Nov 2023, $40M plus up to $35M milestones; Nevro -> Globus, closed 3 Apr 2025, ~$250M); current Globus branding and catalog status of the allograft not confirmed.

evidence.title: Post-market multicenter study of the Nevro1 SI transfixing and fusion system
evidence.finding: Completed May 2025; results not posted; titanium transfixing device, not the allograft.

bd.reimbursement: CPT 27278 (intra-articular, no cortical piercing) unless a cortical-piercing variant or hybrid (27279); ASC device-intensive 2026; non-covered by CGS/Noridian/Palmetto LCDs (transfixation required); implant packaged, no separate HCPCS.
bd.notes: Globus now owns both a lateral HA-coated screw line (SI-LOK/SI-LOK SELECT) and the Vyrsa posterior portfolio; Globus product pages name no graft brand for either, so the Osteocel-with-SI-LOK pairing in the brief is unverified.

ownership_history: Vyrsa Technologies (founded 2021) -> Nevro Corp (30 Nov 2023) -> Globus Medical (3 Apr 2025).
challenge: Vyrsa Pro's current availability under Globus, tissue bank and procedure volumes are not public.

name: iFuse INTRA V and iFuse INTRA X Allograft Implant Systems
composition: INTRA V (formerly INTRA): single triangular cortical allograft; INTRA X: two small cylindrical bone allografts; both 'implantable bone products manufactured from sterilized recovered cadaveric bone tissue', placed intra-articularly through a ~2 cm posterior incision.

on_label_indications: Homologous use: structural allograft bone placed in the sacroiliac joint (HCT/P, no FDA-cleared indication)

applications.evidence_summary: No clinical study retrieved; SI-BONE's product pages cite only finite-element analysis of SI joint motion and state the results are 'not necessarily indicative of human clinical results'. The FY2025 10-K attributes reduced INTRA X demand to the 2024-2025 MAC LCDs precluding coverage of CPT 27278.
applications.caveats: Launched 2024 as a defensive entry into the interventional-pain posterior segment; no SI-BONE-sponsored trial lists the allograft products (NCT07565545 is the titanium INTRA Ti). Manufactured and distributed as HCT/Ps by an undisclosed third-party tissue bank.

evidence.title: iFuse INTRA Ti (titanium posterior-inferior intra-articular cortical-piercing implant) safety and effectiveness
evidence.finding: Not yet recruiting (start Sep 2026); titanium successor billed under 27279, not the allograft.

bd.reimbursement: CPT 27278 (intra-articular, no cortical piercing) unless a cortical-piercing variant or hybrid (27279); ASC device-intensive 2026; non-covered by CGS/Noridian/Palmetto LCDs (transfixation required); implant packaged, no separate HCPCS.
bd.notes: 10-K: 'Our iFuse INTRA/INTRA X implants are derived from human bone tissue ... manufactured and distributed by a third-party as HCT/P products'; 10-K maps INTRA X to CPT 27278 ($441 facility / $13,834 OBL physician fee 2026) and the titanium products to 27279. SI-BONE sells direct (89 territory managers, 83 clinical specialists, 320 agents, FY2025).

challenge: Tissue bank not named; no clinical data; the 2024 launch year comes from the 10-K product chronology, not a dated release.

name: Actifuse (ABX, Flow, Shape, Mis System) silicate-substituted calcium phosphate
ownership_history: Developed by ApaTech (UK); Baxter acquired ApaTech for $330 million in 2010 and continues to list Actifuse and Altapore under Baxter Advanced Surgery (no divestiture found through 2025).
composition: Silicate-substituted calcium phosphate (0.8 wt% silicon in hydroxyapatite), 80% porosity granules; Flow and Shape add a polymer/aqueous carrier

regulatory.reference: K082575 (ApaTech, cleared 2008-11-25; spine including posterolateral fusion with stabilizing hardware); K090850 (dental, 2009); later Baxter clearances for Actifuse Flow/Shape and Altapore (2018)
on_label_indications: Packed gently into bony voids or gaps of the skeletal system including the spine, and in posterolateral fusion procedures with appropriate stabilizing hardware (K082575)

applications.evidence_summary: Small Australian RCT (Licina 2015, n=19): Actifuse 9/9 vs Infuse 8/9 fused at 12 months with similar clinical outcomes.
applications.caveats: n=19, single center; underpowered to show noninferiority.

evidence.title: Comparison of silicate-substituted calcium phosphate (Actifuse) with rhBMP-2 (Infuse) in posterolateral instrumented lumbar fusion
evidence.finding: Fusion 9/9 (SiCaP) vs 8/9 (rhBMP-2); comparable pain and QoL.

bd.reimbursement: Bundled in fusion MS-DRGs.
bd.notes: Baxter Advanced Surgery sells direct; Actifuse is a small line inside a large surgical-sealant portfolio and periodically appears on divestiture speculation lists, but no sale was found.

name: CERAMENT Bone Void Filler
company: BONESUPPORT AB (Lund, Sweden; Nasdaq Stockholm: BONEX)
ownership_history: Founded 1999 from Lund University research; independent public company since 2017 IPO.
composition: Injectable biphasic ceramic: 60% calcium sulfate hemihydrate and 40% hydroxyapatite, mixed with iohexol as radiocontrast; sets in situ, drillable, resorbs as calcium sulfate dissolves and HA is remodeled.

on_label_indications: Ceramic bone graft substitute for bony voids or gaps in the extremities, pelvis and posterolateral spine (open surgery only) and intervertebral disc space, including benign bone cysts and tumors and osseous defects from surgery or trauma
Resorbs and is replaced by bone; can be drilled and used with screws; provides no structural support during healing

applications.evidence_summary: Retrospective 13-patient series of depressed metaphyseal fractures (none distal femur) showed no loss of reduction at 6 months (Yeo 2018). A 137-patient RCT versus autograft in tibial plateau fractures (NCT01828905, Mainz) is complete; femur-specific data absent.
applications.caveats: Evidence is small and off-site (tibial plateau, calcaneus).

applications.evidence_summary: Two small academic pilots (NCT04498715 Lithuania, NCT06135298 Turkey) tested Cerament BVF injected around sliding hip screws or nails plus zoledronate; no results published.
applications.caveats: Pilot studies of 20 patients; not a commercial indication.

applications.evidence_summary: Used to backfill the decompression track with or without BMAC in case series; no RCT.
applications.caveats: Competes with Pro-Dense kit, which has a dedicated core-decompression 510(k).

applications.evidence_summary: CERTiFy (Hofmann 2020, n=135, 20 German centers, NCT01828905) randomized OTA 41-B2/B3 fractures to ICBG or CERAMENT BVF: noninferior on SF-12 PCS and pain at 26 weeks, less blood loss and day-1 pain, equal healing, remodeling and subsidence.
applications.caveats: Sponsor-funded; open-label; German sites; primary endpoint is quality of life not subsidence; 26-week horizon.

applications.evidence_summary: On-label by site; no pilon data.
applications.caveats: None found.

applications.evidence_summary: Injectable CS/HA fill of the osteotomy gap is reported in small European series; no RCT.
applications.caveats: Thin evidence.

applications.evidence_summary: Positioned for plateau and calcaneal void fill and for benign cysts; no calcaneus-specific clinical series found in this sweep.
applications.caveats: Evidence gap for the plain BVF in the foot.

applications.evidence_summary: Prospective cohort of 24 proximal humerus ORIFs augmented with CERAMENT BVF, propensity-matched 1:1 to unaugmented controls: union 92% vs 83% (ns), screw penetration 4% vs 21% (p=0.08), revision 4% vs 17% (ns); multivariate OR for screw penetration 0.007 (Sinkler 2025, PMID:40885162).
applications.caveats: Small single-center cohort, retrospective comparator, wide confidence intervals; no RCT.

applications.evidence_summary: No distal radius clinical data found; biomechanical augmentation work only (Kok 2019/2022).
applications.caveats: No clinical evidence in the wrist.

evidence.title: Use of a biphasic cement bone substitute in the management of metaphyseal fractures.
evidence.finding: No significant collapse of reduction at 6 months in depressed metaphyseal fractures filled with Cerament BVF.

evidence.title: Prospective multicenter randomized study of CERAMENT BVF versus autologous cancellous bone graft in tibia plateau fractures
evidence.finding: Completed 2017 (Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz); publication not located in this sweep.

evidence.title: Autologous iliac bone graft compared with biphasic hydroxyapatite and calcium sulfate cement for bone defects in tibial plateau fractures: prospective, randomized, open-label, multicenter study (CERTiFy)
evidence.finding: Noninferiority of CBVF to ICBG on SF-12 PCS and VAS at week 26 met; significantly less blood loss (p=0.007) and day-1 pain (p=0.008); no difference in healing, remodeling or subsidence. Level I.

evidence.title: CERTiFy protocol (Trials 2014)
evidence.finding: Protocol: 13 German centers, AO 41-B2/B3, primary SF-12 PCS at 26 weeks, NCT01828905.

evidence.title: Radiographic and histological analysis of a synthetic bone graft substitute eluting gentamicin in the treatment of chronic osteomyelitis
evidence.finding: Mean void filling 73.8% with the biphasic carrier (gentamicin version) at a mean 1.7 years; histology shows osteoconduction and remodeling.

evidence.title: Outcomes of proximal humerus ORIF augmented with calcium sulfate hydroxyapatite bio-composite (CERAMENT BONE VOID FILLER)
evidence.finding: Lower screw penetration and revision in the augmented group; differences not statistically significant except on multivariate analysis.

bd.reimbursement: Bundled in inpatient MS-DRG; Bonesupport runs a US 'Reimbursement Programs' page, which signals that outpatient packaging is a sales obstacle it actively manages.
bd.notes: Bonesupport moved to a direct US sales force after ending its Zimmer Biomet distribution deal in 2017-2018 (see notes file; not re-verified here). Cerament BVF is the on-ramp; Cerament G is the growth product.

name: CERAMENT G (gentamicin-eluting)
ownership_history: Same as Cerament BVF.
composition: Cerament biphasic ceramic (60% calcium sulfate, 40% hydroxyapatite) premixed with gentamicin sulfate (17.5 mg per mL); device-drug combination product regulated by CDRH.

regulatory.reference: DEN210044 (granted May 17, 2022; product code QRR, 21 CFR 888.3046); follow-on 510(k) K234008 (March 13, 2024) extended the indication to open fractures
on_label_indications: Resorbable, gentamicin-eluting ceramic bone void filler for defects in the extremities of skeletally mature patients as an adjunct to systemic antibiotic therapy and surgical debridement as part of the standard treatment approach to bone infection and open fractures (K234008 wording)

Can reduce the occurrence and reoccurrence of bone infection from gentamicin-sensitive organisms to protect bone healing; may augment provisional hardware; not intended to provide structural support during healing

applications.evidence_summary: The FORTIFY RCT (NCT02820363, 201 open tibial fractures, US and Europe) met its safety endpoint but the composite efficacy endpoint (no deep infection and no secondary procedure to promote union at 12 months) was 64% with Cerament G versus 66% control, not significant, with only 143 of 201 evaluable; Bonesupport called it 'inconclusive' and it did not support a PMA. The 2024 510(k) nonetheless added 'open fractures' to the label on a De Novo-based substantial-equivalence argument. Observational registries (NCT06010433) and a 220-patient French RCT in chronic osteomyelitis (CONVICTION, NCT04805164) are running.
applications.caveats: Pivotal trauma RCT was negative/inconclusive; infection-indication evidence is largely single-arm; sponsor-funded.

applications.evidence_summary: McNally 2016 (Oxford, n=100, 105 bones, mean follow-up 19.5 months) single-stage protocol with CERAMENT G: infection eradicated in 96%, 10 infected nonunions included; the De Novo cited this plus animal and bench data. A 220-patient French RCT (CONVICTION, NCT04805164) and a Bonesupport post-market cohort (NCT06555848) are ongoing.
applications.caveats: Pivotal human evidence is a prospective single-arm series from an expert unit; no RCT has read out; wound leakage is the recurring complication of calcium sulfate carriers.

applications.evidence_summary: Covered by the bone-infection indication; infected nonunions formed 10% of the McNally cohort; Lyon Masquelet series used CERAMENT G and V as the stage-one spacer adjunct (NCT03970941, n=8).
applications.caveats: Small numbers for the nonunion subset.

applications.evidence_summary: FORTIFY (NCT02820363, n=201, Gustilo II-IIIB tibial shaft with 3-27.5 mm gap, 31 sites US/EU) was inconclusive: 12-month composite success 64% CERAMENT G vs 66% control, non-significant, 29% dropout, safety endpoint met; the company then obtained the open-fracture indication through a 510(k) in 2024 rather than PMA, and CMS granted an NTAP for open fractures from 2025-10-01.
applications.caveats: Negative/inconclusive RCT underpins an indication cleared by substantial equivalence; a trauma biologics manager will ask what clinical data justify the open-fracture claim beyond safety.
applications.challenge: FORTIFY failed its primary endpoint; the open-fracture indication rests on the De Novo predicate plus safety, not efficacy.

applications.evidence_summary: McNally 2016 (PMID 27587534): prospective series of 100 patients with Cierny-Mader III/IV chronic osteomyelitis treated single-stage; infection eradicated in 96 with one procedure. McNally 2022 (PMID 36047024): same cohort at mean 6 years, 94% infection-free. Ferguson 2023 (PMID 37400090): 180 CERAMENT G vs 179 tobramycin calcium-sulfate pellets, recurrence 4.4% vs 11.2%.
applications.caveats: Oxford Bone Infection Unit series, predominantly long-bone and not diabetic-foot cohorts; no RCT in diabetic foot yet (ACHILLS RCT NCT07057817 in calcaneal osteomyelitis started 2026; Groningen DFU-osteomyelitis cohort NCT05316298). The label covers extremity bone infection generally, so diabetic-foot use is on-label but its specific evidence base is thin.

applications.evidence_summary: Infected Charcot reconstruction is a natural use under the bone-infection label; no Charcot-specific series found.
applications.caveats: Evidence gap.

applications.evidence_summary: NCT02820363: 201-patient multicenter RCT of CERAMENT G as part of surgical repair of open diaphyseal tibial fractures, completed 2021; supported the 2024 open-fracture label expansion (results not retrieved with a PMID in this sweep).
applications.caveats: Tibial shaft, not ankle; applies to open ankle/pilon fractures only by label extension.

applications.evidence_summary: Prospective single-stage series of 100 patients / 105 bones with chronic osteomyelitis: infection eradicated in 96% with one procedure, 19.5-month mean follow-up (McNally 2016, PMID:27587534). K234008 cites a Manchester open-fracture cohort (2013-2021) with 3.7% deep infection, 96.3% limb salvage and 96% union vs literature standard of care. Upper-extremity bones are a minority in both.
applications.caveats: No RCT yet; the French CONVICTION RCT (NCT04805164, n=220, primary endpoint cost-utility) completes 2027. Company-sponsored US registry NCT06010433 and single-stage cohort NCT06555848 ongoing. Humerus cases appear only as a handful in open-fracture series (Sandilands 2026, PMID:41800468).

evidence.title: FORTIFY: Prospective randomized multicenter controlled trial of CERAMENT G as part of surgical repair of open diaphyseal tibial fractures
evidence.finding: Composite efficacy success 64% versus 66% (not significant); primary safety endpoint met; high dropout (143 evaluable) made the study unsuitable for PMA.

evidence.title: CONVICTION: randomized multicenter study of Cerament G in chronic osteomyelitis of long bones (CRIOAc network)
evidence.finding: Recruiting; primary completion expected November 2027.

evidence.title: Single-stage treatment of chronic osteomyelitis with a new absorbable, gentamicin-loaded, calcium sulphate/hydroxyapatite biocomposite: a prospective series of 100 cases
evidence.finding: Multidisciplinary single-stage protocol (debridement, culture-directed systemic antibiotics, stabilization, CERAMENT G dead-space fill, primary closure); infection eradicated in 96 of 100 at mean 19.5 months; 80% Cierny-Mader class B hosts.

evidence.title: Outcomes and safety of antibiotic-loaded calcium sulfate beads in orthopaedics: systematic review and meta-analysis
evidence.finding: 41 studies, no RCTs; pooled osteomyelitis eradication 88%, infected-nonunion union 93%; wound complications 17% in osteomyelitis cases.

evidence.title: Mid- to long-term results of single-stage surgery for patients with chronic osteomyelitis using a bioabsorbable gentamicin-loaded ceramic carrier
evidence.finding: 94% infection-free at mean 6.05 years; recurrence unrelated to host class or gentamicin resistance.

evidence.title: A comparison of clinical and radiological outcomes between two different biodegradable local antibiotic carriers used in the single-stage surgical management of long bone osteomyelitis
evidence.finding: Lower recurrence, leakage and fracture, and better void filling (73.9% vs 40.0%) than calcium-sulfate pellets.

evidence.title: ACHILLS: partial calcanectomy plus antibiotic-impregnated bone graft substitute vs partial calcanectomy alone for calcaneal osteomyelitis
evidence.finding: Recruiting (Royal College of Surgeons in Ireland), start January 2026; first RCT in a diabetic calcaneal-osteomyelitis population.

evidence.title: Post-market prospective cohort of CERAMENT G in single-stage surgical treatment of osteomyelitis
evidence.finding: BONESUPPORT post-market study started June 2025.

evidence.title: Intramedullary nailing with absorbable antibiotic-eluting ceramic for FRI prophylaxis in high-risk open fractures
evidence.finding: Nine open tibia/femur/humerus fractures nailed with Cerament G delivered intramedullary; all united, no FRI at 9 months.

pipeline.expected_milestone: CONVICTION RCT primary completion November 2027 (ClinicalTrials.gov)

bd.reimbursement: Inpatient: bundled in MS-DRG (osteomyelitis and open-fracture DRGs). Bonesupport has pursued separate payment mechanisms and markets a reimbursement support program; whether any NTAP or pass-through was obtained was not verified in this sweep.
bd.notes: First FDA-authorized antibiotic-eluting bone void filler; Breakthrough Device designation. The pricing model is premium versus Stimulan (surgeon-mixed antibiotic, cheaper) and PMMA beads (off-label antibiotic loading, cheapest). Bonesupport's US revenue growth 2023-2025 is driven by this product per its public reports (not re-verified here).
bd.challenge: An NTAP claim without the CMS final-rule citation will be challenged; verify before using in a pitch.

name: MagnetOs (Granules, Putty, Easypack Putty, Flex Matrix)
ownership_history: Technology from Xpand Biotechnology (Netherlands; AttraX predicate); Kuros Biosciences (SIX: KURN) acquired Xpand in 2016. Kuros remains independent; On 2025-01-07 Kuros Biosciences USA, Inc. announced a five-year exclusive sales agency agreement under which Medtronic's spinal division acts as exclusive sales agent for MagnetOs in mutually agreed US spine territories, converting an earlier trial arrangement into a strategic alliance. Per the Kuros investor release as summarized by search (the IR page returned HTTP 403 to direct fetch; the structure and term are mirrored by BoneZone and Medical Design & Development), Kuros keeps contracts, hospital partnerships and revenue recognition and may sell directly in non-contracted territories and non-spine markets. No financial terms were disclosed. No Globus Medical acquisition occurred (Globus's 2025 deal was Nevro).
composition: Biphasic calcium phosphate (65-70% beta-TCP / 30-35% hydroxyapatite) with a submicron, needle-shaped surface topography ('NeedleGrip'); Putty/Easypack add a resorbable polymer binder; Flex Matrix is a collagen-based strip

regulatory.reference: openFDA (FDA 510(k) database) MagnetOs entries: K161859 (MagnetOs, Xpand Biotechnology BV, 2017-02-24); K171563 (Putty, 2017-08-24); K181958 (Putty, 2018-12-06); K211201 (Easypack Putty, 2021-09-02); K213111 (Granules, 2022-01-10); K213959 (Flex Matrix, 2022-04-14); K230736 (Putty, 2023-12-20); K233245 (Flex Matrix, 2023-11-21); K233607 (Easypack Putty, 2023-12-15); K232347 (Granules, 2024-01-19); K240442 (Putty, 2024-04-01); K241212 (Easypack Putty, 2024-06-27); K243474 (MagnetOs MIS, 2025-05-23); applicant Kuros Biosciences B.V. (Xpand earlier). All product code MQV bone void fillers.; openFDA: K230736 (MagnetOs Putty, 2023-12-20); K233607 (Easypack Putty, 2023-12-15); K232347 (Granules, 2024-01-19); K240442 (Putty, 2024-04-01); K241212 (Easypack Putty, 2024-06-27); K243474 (MagnetOs MIS, 2025-05-23). Applicant Kuros Biosciences B.V.
on_label_indications: Bone void filler for voids or gaps not intrinsic to the stability of the bony structure; posterolateral spine (extender and, for Granules/Putty, standalone); interbody use with a cleared cage (Easypack Putty, Granules, Flex Matrix). Not cleared as osteoinductive by FDA or TGA.

applications.evidence_summary: Dutch multicenter intra-patient RCT (Stempels 2024, NCT03625544, n=100, 128 segments): 1-year CT fusion 79% on the MagnetOs Granules side vs 47% on the autograft side, noninferior and indicating superiority. Ongoing: Easypack Putty standalone vs DBM+local bone (NCT04679844, n=60), Flex Matrix + local bone vs Trinity ELITE (NCT05037968, n=100), Flex Matrix vs cellular allograft observational (NCT06415123), Putty vs local autograft up to 3 levels (NCT04679896, n=30, completed).
applications.caveats: Investigator-sponsored with Kuros as collaborator; the surprisingly low autograft-side fusion (47%) is a per-side CT metric that makes the delta look larger than clinical nonunion rates; the osteoinductive mechanism (M2 macrophage polarization) is a company claim supported by preclinical work and is not an FDA-cleared claim.

applications.evidence_summary: Interbody clearance (2024) for Easypack Putty, Granules and Flex Matrix with cleared cages; no interbody clinical outcomes published.
applications.caveats: Interbody evidence gap; a single-arm LLIF study (NCT04128852) was withdrawn.

applications.evidence_summary: The MaxA RCT enrolled deformity and up-to-6-level constructs (T10-S2), so part of the evidence applies to longer fusions; a 140-patient adolescent idiopathic scoliosis intra-patient RCT (NCT07512336, UMC Utrecht) starts 2026.
applications.caveats: Subgroup data not published separately.

applications.evidence_summary: NCT07225751: prospective, randomized, single-blind, multicenter study of MagnetOs vs autogenous bone graft in hindfoot or ankle fusion, 126 patients, 7 sites, started 2025-11-25, primary completion October 2028. The first randomized autograft-controlled synthetic trial in the foot since Augment.
applications.caveats: No foot/ankle results yet; spine evidence is the basis for the claim.

applications.evidence_summary: Covered by the same trial (NCT07225751).
applications.caveats: As above.

evidence.title: Efficacy of biphasic calcium phosphate ceramic with a needle-shaped surface topography versus autograft in instrumented posterolateral spinal fusion
evidence.finding: Per-side 1-year CT fusion 79% MagnetOs vs 47% autograft (difference 32 points, 95% CI 23-41); noninferiority met.

evidence.title: MagnetOs Flex Matrix mixed with local autograft vs Trinity Elite mixed with local autograft in up to four-level instrumented PLF
evidence.finding: Recruiting; primary completion December 2026; first head-to-head of a ceramic vs a cellular allograft.

evidence.title: MagnetOs Easypack Putty standalone vs DBX/Grafton mixed with local autograft in 1-2 level instrumented PLF
evidence.finding: Recruiting; primary completion June 2027.

evidence.title: MagnetOs compared to autogenous bone graft in patients undergoing hindfoot or ankle fusions
evidence.finding: Recruiting; Kuros-sponsored.

evidence.title: Randomized intra-patient controlled trial of MagnetOs granules vs autograft in instrumented posterolateral spinal fusion
evidence.finding: Completed October 2023; spine.

bd.reimbursement: Bundled in fusion MS-DRGs; no separate payment.
bd.notes: Kuros IR (Jan 7, 2025 release): five-year exclusive sales agency agreement under which Medtronic's spine division sells MagnetOs in mutually agreed US spine territories; Kuros supports Medtronic's sales force but keeps responsibility for contracts, hospital partnerships and revenue recognition, and continues to sell directly in non-contracted territories and outside spine; the deal converted an initial trial agreement. FY2025 (Mar 10, 2026 release): group revenue USD 146.1M (+72%), direct MagnetOs sales USD 143.9M (+71%), first net profit USD 2.6M, 2026 guidance at least 35% growth, 2028 target USD 300-330M; a 510(k) for the MagnetOs MIS Delivery System is cited without a date; the release states MagnetOs is not FDA cleared as an osteoinductive bone graft.

challenge: Medtronic agreement terms and FY2025 revenue (USD 146.1M; MagnetOs 143.9M) read from Kuros IR pages 2026-10-22. 510(k) numbers confirmed in openFDA (K230736, K233607, K232347, K240442, K241212, K243474). The 'osteoinductive' language is marketing; FDA cleared MagnetOs as an osteoconductive bone void filler.

pipeline.expected_milestone: Hindfoot/ankle RCT primary completion October 2028 (ClinicalTrials.gov); product is already marketable under 510(k), so the trial is for claims and adoption rather than approval.

name: Mastergraft (Granules, Matrix, Putty, Strip)
ownership_history: Medtronic Sofamor Danek original product line (first clearance 2002).
composition: Biphasic calcium phosphate (15% hydroxyapatite / 85% beta-TCP) granules; Matrix/Putty/Strip combine the ceramic with bovine type I collagen

on_label_indications: Bone void filler for voids or gaps not intrinsic to the stability of the bony structure in the extremities, pelvis and posterolateral spine, as an autograft extender (per Mastergraft family labeling; verify form-specific wording)

applications.evidence_summary: No peer-reviewed comparative clinical study of Mastergraft retrieved; it is the ceramic extender most often paired with Infuse in Medtronic constructs and is the ceramic component of the rhBMP-2/CRM (Amplify) carrier studied by Dimar 2009.
applications.caveats: Evidence gap for the standalone product.

bd.reimbursement: Bundled in fusion MS-DRGs.
bd.notes: Medtronic direct reps; frequently bundled with Infuse kits in pricing conversations.

name: Opening-wedge osteotomy ceramic wedges (Arthrex HATriC, OSferion; Cross.Bone)
ownership_history: HATriC cleared to Arthrex 2004 (K040381); OSferion (Olympus Terumo Biomaterials beta-TCP) distributed by Arthrex as an osteotomy wedge; Cross.Bone wedge K071876.
composition: HATriC: 60% HA / 40% beta-TCP biphasic ceramic wedge; OSferion: 100% high-purity beta-TCP wedge

regulatory.reference: K040381 (HATriC, 2004-05-12); K071876 (Cross.Bone wedge, tibial osteotomy with internal fixation); OSferion wedge K number not retrieved
on_label_indications: Bone void filler or bone graft substitute in bony voids or gaps not intrinsic to the stability of the bony structure (extremities, pelvis, spine); not a load-bearing device; use with adequate post-operative immobilization (HATriC)

applications.evidence_summary: Beta-TCP and HA/TCP wedges fill large opening-wedge gaps with locking plates; meta-analyses show no overall nonunion difference vs no filler or graft, and a 2026 systematic review of 1,640 knees found no outcome benefit from any filler for gaps under 10 mm. A 2026 bilateral-knee RCT (n=42) found TCP granules gave better WOMAC/VAS than allograft.
applications.caveats: Clearance is for a void filler with a 'not load-bearing' statement, while the clinical use is structural gap support under a plate; cleared without clinical data.

evidence.title: The use of bone void fillers may not impact outcomes after medial opening wedge HTO: systematic review
evidence.finding: 28 studies; 36% allograft, 30% no filler, 22% synthetic, 12% autograft; no outcome difference; fillers may add complications for gaps under 10 mm.

evidence.title: Allogenous bone graft versus synthetic calcium-phosphate graft in opening wedge HTO
evidence.finding: 84 knees (bilateral), randomized by knee; TCP granules superior on WOMAC and VAS at 2.1 years; consolidation 54.8%; no loss of correction.

bd.reimbursement: Bundled inpatient MS-DRG or packaged into the outpatient osteotomy APC (HTO is increasingly outpatient).
bd.notes: Sold as a system accessory with Arthrex's osteotomy plates; evidence says the plate, not the wedge, is doing the work.

name: Osteopore PCL Scaffold Bone Filler (Osteoplug, Osteoplug-C, Osteomesh)
composition: 3D-printed bioresorbable polycaprolactone scaffold (mushroom-shaped 14 mm burr-hole plug, mesh sheets 50 x 50 x 1 mm) with 400 to 600 micron pores; resorbs over 18 to 24 months

regulatory.reference: K051093 (Osteopore, Inc., Osteopore PCL Scaffold, 2006-03-17, product code GXP)
on_label_indications: Repair of neurosurgical burr holes, craniotomy cuts and other cranial defects; augmentation or restoration of bony contour in the craniofacial skeleton

applications.evidence_summary: 12-patient Singapore series of Osteoplug after chronic subdural hematoma drainage: no depressions, no infection, osteointegration on CT at one year, mean 16 months follow-up.
applications.caveats: No comparative study; US sales small and through a non-exclusive distributor.

evidence.title: Use of Osteoplug polycaprolactone implants as novel burr-hole covers
evidence.finding: Good cosmesis in all 12 patients, radiographic osteointegration at one year, no infection or adverse systemic reaction at mean 16 months.

bd.reimbursement: Bundled.
bd.notes: Zimmer Biomet holds exclusive craniofacial distribution for EMEA and APAC (24 countries, signed July 2024, five-year term; sales began in Europe, Australia and Hong Kong, three-fold unit growth 2024 H2 to 2025 H1; Saudi access July 2026). US distribution is a separate, non-exclusive two-year agreement with Bioplate for cranial and neurosurgery (date unverified). The TnR clearance used Osteopore as predicate, so a second PCL entrant now competes in the same niche.

name: PRO-DENSE Bone Graft Substitute (and PRO-DENSE Core Decompression Kit, PRO-DENSE LoVisc)
ownership_history: Wright Medical Technology (Memphis/Arlington, TN); Stryker since November 2020.
composition: Injectable triphasic composite of calcium sulfate with brushite and beta-TCP granules (75% calcium sulfate / 25% calcium phosphate) that sets in situ; LoVisc is a lower-viscosity formulation (K200507 2020, K213342 2022).

on_label_indications: Bone graft substitute to be injected or digitally packed into open bone voids/gaps that are not intrinsic to the stability of the bony structure, in the extremities, pelvis and spine
Core Decompression Procedure Kit cleared for delivery into the decompression tract

applications.evidence_summary: Civinini 2012 (37 hips, stages IC-IIIA): core decompression plus BMAC plus Pro-Dense backfill, 86.5% clinical success and 78% radiographic non-progression at a mean 20.6 months; no control arm.
applications.caveats: Single-center, short follow-up, combined with BMAC so the contribution of the filler cannot be isolated.

applications.evidence_summary: Marketed for metaphyseal void fill; no femur-specific data located.
applications.caveats: Class-level use only.

applications.evidence_summary: Marketed for metaphyseal trauma voids on the strength of a canine proximal humerus model and bone-tumor series; no plateau RCT; Wright's brochure itself states canine results may not translate to humans.
applications.caveats: Preclinical plus case-series evidence only for trauma.

applications.evidence_summary: Used as an injectable extender; no nonunion data found.
applications.caveats: Expert opinion.

applications.evidence_summary: Used for calcaneal cyst and post-reduction void fill; Stryker's efficacy claims come from a canine proximal-humerus defect model.
applications.caveats: No clinical foot/ankle series found.

evidence.title: The use of an injectable calcium sulphate/calcium phosphate bioceramic in the treatment of osteonecrosis of the femoral head.
evidence.finding: Harris hip score improved 68 to 86; 29 of 37 hips improved or did not collapse; 3 conversions to THA.

evidence.title: PRO-DENSE 510(k) K182823 summary
evidence.finding: Substantial equivalence with bench and animal data; indication expanded to pediatric patients 6 years and older.

bd.reimbursement: Bundled in inpatient MS-DRG (core decompression of the hip is often inpatient or hospital outpatient; filler packaged into the APC).
bd.notes: The core decompression kit is a niche differentiated SKU: a dedicated 510(k) for a procedure where most competitors sell generic void fillers.

catalog_status_2026: Stryker's US trauma-and-extremities bone grafting catalog page (read 2026-10-22) lists AlloFiber, AlloMatrix, Augment, BIO4, DBM, FusionFlex, HydroSet XT, Ignite, OsteoSet, Pro-Dense, Pro-Dense LoVisc, Pro-Stim, Tensix, Vitoss, Vitoss BA, Vitoss BA2X and Vitoss BBTrauma as current products.

name: Vitoss / Vitoss BA / Vitoss BA2X (beta-TCP with bioactive glass)
ownership_history: Orthovita (Malvern, PA) launched Vitoss in 2000; Stryker completed its acquisition of Orthovita on 2011-06-28 (tender offer at $3.85 per share, agreement dated 2011-05-16, about $316 million).
composition: Ultraporous beta-tricalcium phosphate (nanoscale pores, ~90% porosity) with bovine collagen in Foam/Flow forms; Vitoss BA and BA2X add 45S5 bioactive glass (20% and 2x that amount) to the collagen-TCP composite

regulatory.reference: K083033 (Vitoss, 2008-11-06); K103173 (Vitoss BA BiModal, 2011-02-07); K153608 (BiModal foam strip, 2016-02-12); K163621 (Vitoss BA Injectable, 2017-05-02); K242280 (BiModal foam strip, 2024-08-29); K261008 (BiModal family, 2026-04-24); applicant Orthovita / Stryker Spine; K102545 is a special 510(k) for a Vitoss formulation; openFDA: K083033 (Vitoss BGS and Foam, Orthovita, 2008-11-06); K103173 (Vitoss BA BiModal, 2011-02-07); K153608 (2016); K163621 (Vitoss BA Injectable, 2017-05-02); K242280 (Vitoss family incl. BBTrauma and BA2X, Stryker Spine, 2024-08-29); K261008 (Vitoss family, Stryker Spine, 2026-04-24)
on_label_indications: Bone void filler for voids or gaps not intrinsic to the stability of the bony structure in the extremities, pelvis and posterolateral spine; posterolateral spine use as an autograft extender (typical Vitoss labeling; verify)

applications.evidence_summary: Single-surgeon prospective series with lamina autograft/Vitoss: 100 instrumented PLFs with 3.8% (one-level) and 9.5% (two-level) pseudarthrosis by CT (Epstein 2009); 60 noninstrumented geriatric PLFs with 15% pseudarthrosis (Epstein 2008); 40 instrumented PLFs with 3 pseudarthroses (Epstein 2006). A Chinese RCT of generic beta-TCP + local bone vs ICBG (Dai 2008, n=62) found 100% fusion in both arms.
applications.caveats: No RCT of the Vitoss brand; the Dai RCT used a beta-TCP whose brand is not stated in the abstract; Vitoss BA bioactive glass versions have no published spine RCT.

applications.evidence_summary: Ceramic extenders such as Vitoss are routinely mixed with rhBMP-2 in long constructs; no deformity-specific trial retrieved.
applications.caveats: Practice-pattern inference.

applications.evidence_summary: Marketed for trauma voids (BBTrauma); evidence is class-level from plateau meta-analyses of synthetic fillers versus autograft; no Vitoss-specific RCT in trauma found.
applications.caveats: Non-structural foam; surgeons often pair it with a cement or hardware raft for plateau depression.

applications.evidence_summary: Used as an autograft extender in nonunion and Masquelet second stage; no comparative trauma data found.
applications.caveats: Expert-opinion level.

applications.evidence_summary: Class-level: Lee 2023 (PMID 38018529) retrospective comparison of highly porous beta-TCP plus BMAC vs no graft in midfoot arthrodesis, 44 patients/89 joints; union 91.5% vs 76.2% (p=0.048).
applications.caveats: Brand not stated; BMAC confounds; midfoot arthrodesis for arthritis and deformity, not all Charcot.

applications.evidence_summary: Used as a void filler under the reduced posterior facet; no Vitoss-specific calcaneal series found.
applications.caveats: Granular TCP does not provide the immediate structural support a setting cement does.

applications.evidence_summary: Class evidence only: granular beta-TCP added nothing to angle-stable plating in a 39-patient RCT (Jakubietz 2011, PMID:21600042). No Vitoss-specific wrist trial found.
applications.caveats: Negative class-level result.

applications.evidence_summary: Synthetic void fill for the metaphyseal defect is described in the augmentation literature (Biermann 2019) without Vitoss-specific outcomes.
applications.caveats: No product data.

evidence.title: Beta tricalcium phosphate: observation of use in 100 posterolateral lumbar instrumented fusions
evidence.finding: Pseudarthrosis 3.8% (one-level) and 9.5% (two-level) with lamina autograft/Vitoss by dynamic X-ray and CT.

evidence.title: Noninstrumented posterolateral lumbar fusions in predominantly geriatric patients using lamina autograft and beta tricalcium phosphate
evidence.finding: 15% pseudarthrosis in noninstrumented 1-2 level fusions with Vitoss strips soaked in marrow aspirate.

evidence.title: Single-level instrumented posterolateral fusion of lumbar spine with beta-tricalcium phosphate versus autograft: a prospective, randomized study with 3-year follow-up
evidence.finding: 100% radiographic fusion in both beta-TCP + local bone and ICBG arms; all ICBG patients had donor-site pain.

evidence.title: Surgical fixation methods for tibial plateau fractures (Cochrane review)
evidence.finding: Six trials (368 participants) compared bone substitute vs autograft; all small and at high risk of bias; insufficient evidence to pick the best void filler.

evidence.title: The efficiency of highly porous beta-tricalcium phosphate with bone marrow aspirate concentrate in midfoot joint arthrodesis
evidence.finding: Union 91.5% with beta-TCP plus BMAC vs 76.2% without.

evidence.title: Midfoot joint arthrodesis using compression plate with lag screw augmenting with highly porous beta-TCP and BMAC
evidence.finding: 97.3% joint union (73 of 75 joints).

evidence.title: The use of beta-tricalcium phosphate bone graft substitute in dorsally plated, comminuted distal radius fractures
evidence.finding: No advantage of granular beta-TCP with angle-stable plating.

bd.reimbursement: Bundled in fusion MS-DRGs.
bd.notes: Stryker Spine direct reps; Stryker's biologics bag also includes Bio4 (Osiris/Smith+Nephew manufactured) and Cortoss for VCF.

challenge: Vitoss, Vitoss BA and BA2X are current on Stryker's catalog page (2026-10-22); K numbers still not retrieved (FDA 510(k) search is bot-gated).
catalog_status_2026: Stryker's US trauma-and-extremities bone grafting catalog page (read 2026-10-22) lists AlloFiber, AlloMatrix, Augment, BIO4, DBM, FusionFlex, HydroSet XT, Ignite, OsteoSet, Pro-Dense, Pro-Dense LoVisc, Pro-Stim, Tensix, Vitoss, Vitoss BA, Vitoss BA2X and Vitoss BBTrauma as current products.

name: chronOS beta-TCP (granules, blocks, Strip, Vivify)
ownership_history: Developed by Synthes/Mathys (Switzerland); Synthes acquired by Johnson & Johnson in 2012 and merged into DePuy Synthes.
composition: Pure-phase beta-tricalcium phosphate, 60% porosity with interconnected 100-500 micron pores; chronOS Strip combines beta-TCP granules with a polylactide-co-caprolactone polymer; chronOS Vivify adds collagen

regulatory.reference: K013072 (chronOS TCP, 2002-11-26); K041350 (chronOS, 2004-07-08); K043045 (chronOS, 2005-01-07; may be combined with autogenous blood/marrow); K053022 (chronOS beta-TCP, 2006-01-23); K071046 (chronOS Composite, 2007-10-23); applicant Synthes (USA)
on_label_indications: Bone void filler for voids or gaps that are not intrinsic to the stability of the bony structure; gently packed into bony voids or gaps of the skeletal system (extremities, spine and pelvis); may be combined with autogenous blood and/or bone marrow (K043045)

applications.evidence_summary: The best RCT for beta-TCP as a local-bone extender in instrumented PLF (Dai 2008, n=62) showed 100% fusion in both the beta-TCP and ICBG arms at 3 years with no donor-site pain in the TCP arm; brand of beta-TCP not specified in the abstract.
applications.caveats: Small single-center RCT, fusion by plain radiograph; the K013072 label does not say 'posterolateral' explicitly.

applications.evidence_summary: Beta-TCP granules are among the synthetic fillers pooled in plateau meta-analyses (Cooper 2022: 6 RCTs, 353 fractures, synthetics equal to autograft on depression with less blood loss and shorter surgery); no chronOS-specific plateau RCT found.
applications.caveats: Class-level evidence; granular TCP offers less immediate structural support than cement.

applications.evidence_summary: Beta-TCP wedges and granules are the most studied synthetic HTO fillers (Bei 2022 meta-analysis: 5 RCTs, 8 NRS, 769 patients; no difference in nonunion overall but higher nonunion when combined with long locking plates). chronOS wedge is sold ex-US; US HTO wedges with 510(k) are Arthrex HATriC and OSferion.
applications.caveats: chronOS HTO wedge US clearance not confirmed; evidence is class-level.

applications.evidence_summary: Used as a resorbable void filler after calcaneal and tibial-plateau reduction; no chronOS-specific calcaneal outcome study found.
applications.caveats: Evidence gap.

applications.evidence_summary: Preformed beta-TCP wedges are one option for Cotton and Evans opening-wedge osteotomies.
applications.caveats: No comparative data.

applications.evidence_summary: Granular beta-TCP added to dorsal angle-stable plating gave no functional, radiographic or complication difference in a 39-patient RCT (Jakubietz 2011, PMID:21600042).
applications.caveats: Small, dorsal plating (now uncommon); negative result.

applications.evidence_summary: Synthetic void fillers appear in the augmentation systematic review (Biermann 2019, PMID:30903343) with level II-IV clinical data; the 2026 RCT meta-analysis found synthetic graft reduced complications but, unlike biologic graft, did not shorten healing time or reduce pain (Daher 2026, PMID:42750779).
applications.caveats: Product-specific proximal humerus data for chronOS not found.

applications.evidence_summary: Cleared for craniofacial defects and craniotomy openings to 25 cm2 on substantial equivalence; no chronOS-named cranial clinical series located.
applications.caveats: Granular beta-TCP lacks the cohesion of a cement and needs containment.

applications.evidence_summary: Dental 510(k) with no clinical data; beta-TCP in sinus lifts is supported by generic beta-TCP literature rather than chronOS trials.
applications.caveats: Commodity.

applications.evidence_summary: A 2023 systematic review of beta-TCP as alveolar cleft graft found only small series and no RCT against iliac crest.
applications.caveats: Off-label in children; no brand-specific data.

evidence.title: Single-level instrumented posterolateral fusion with beta-tricalcium phosphate versus autograft: prospective randomized study, 3-year follow-up
evidence.finding: Equivalent fusion and outcomes; eliminated iliac crest harvest morbidity.

evidence.title: Autologous versus synthetic bone grafts for the surgical management of tibial plateau fractures: systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs
evidence.finding: Six RCTs; no significant difference in articular depression; synthetic grafts had 90 mL less blood loss and 16 min shorter surgery; other outcomes comparable.

evidence.title: Effectiveness of bone substitute materials in opening wedge high tibial osteotomy: systematic review and meta-analysis
evidence.finding: Bone substitutes safe for gaps over 10 mm with locking plates; no overall nonunion difference; low-quality evidence.

evidence.title: The use of beta-tricalcium phosphate bone graft substitute in dorsally plated, comminuted distal radius fractures
evidence.finding: No advantage of additional granular bone graft substitute with angle-stable plating.

evidence.title: Bone graft augmentation reduces complications in osteosynthesis of proximal humerus fractures: a meta-analysis of RCTs
evidence.finding: Five RCTs; graft augmentation lowered complication odds (OR 0.21); synthetic subgroup did not improve healing time or pain.

evidence.title: Beta-tricalcium phosphate as alveolar bone grafting in cleft lip and palate: systematic review
evidence.finding: Small heterogeneous studies; beta-TCP alone or with autograft produced bone fill but without controlled comparison to iliac crest.

bd.reimbursement: Bundled in fusion MS-DRGs.
bd.notes: DePuy Synthes direct force; the company's spine biologics bag is DBX (MTF), ViviGen (LifeNet), chronOS and FIBERGRAFT (Prosidyan, promoted under an exclusive US agreement since 2018).

name: Induce XT (Natural Matrix Protein allograft)
ownership_history: Red Rock Regeneration (private); NMP technology also described in a 2026 preclinical paper (PMID 42774656) from an affiliated group.
composition: Human cortical bone fibers and microparticulates processed into Natural Matrix Protein (NMP, a growth-factor-bioavailability-enhanced demineralized allograft) with added cancellous microparticulates

regulatory.reference: No FDA clearance or approval record found: openFDA 510(k) search for applicant 'Red Rock' returns nothing, and no HCT/P determination is public. Product is a human cortical fiber/microparticulate allograft processed into Natural Matrix Protein (NMP); the prospective foot-and-ankle fusion study NCT06662266 (n=60, started May 2025, est. completion 2027-11) is registered as not an FDA-regulated device study.
on_label_indications: No FDA-reviewed indication; homologous bone-graft use (presumed)

applications.evidence_summary: NCT06662266: prospective single-site evaluation of Induce XT in 60 foot and ankle fusions, enrolling by invitation since May 2025, primary completion November 2026.
applications.caveats: Single-arm, single-site; preclinical claim that NMP releases more BMP-7 than conventional DBM comes from the developer.

evidence.title: Prospective evaluation of Induce XT bone graft in foot and ankle fusion
evidence.finding: Enrolling by invitation.

evidence.title: A novel growth factor bioavailability-enhanced allograft for use in craniomaxillofacial bone regeneration
evidence.finding: NMP released more BMP-7 than DBM and was osteoinductive in the rat muscle pouch; competitors OsteoAMP, OsteoFactor and i-FACTOR did not form bone.

pipeline.expected_milestone: Foot/ankle series readout after November 2026 (ClinicalTrials.gov).

bd.reimbursement: No separate payment; bundled or packaged.
bd.notes: Small-company entrant; relevance is as a signal that 'enhanced DBM' claims are being tested in the foot first because the fusion model is small and outpatient.

challenge: Regulatory pathway (510(k) vs 361) is unstated by the sponsor; no FDA record exists, so the atlas should show it as unclassified/investigational rather than as a 361 product.

name: BRTX-100 (autologous hypoxia-cultured bone marrow MSCs)
ownership_history: Nasdaq: BRTX; public offering (Form 424B4) in 2026.
composition: Autologous bone-marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells culture-expanded under hypoxic conditions, single intradiscal injection in a carrier

regulatory.reference: IND; Fast Track designation for chronic lumbar disc disease (company). Separate IND cleared for chronic cervical discogenic pain (company boilerplate).

applications.evidence_summary: Phase 2 (NCT04042844, n=99 planned, saline-controlled) remains blinded; company presented pooled blinded data at ISCT May 2026 showing 52% of 25 evaluable patients with at least 50% improvement in both VAS and ODI at 52 weeks and no dose-limiting toxicity.
applications.caveats: Blinded, pooled, company-reported interim data from 25 patients cannot show efficacy; no unblinded topline yet; evidence grade will be I only after unblinding of the randomized comparison.

evidence.title: Phase 2, double-blind, randomized, saline-controlled study of a single intradiscal injection of BRTX-100 in chronic lumbar disc disease
evidence.finding: Recruiting/enrolling at 19 sites since June 2022; primary completion Dec 2026; enrollment reported complete (trade press).

pipeline.expected_milestone: Unblinded topline analysis after primary completion (Dec 2026 per registry); company targets a Phase 3 IND submission in late 2026 after a February 2026 Type B meeting (company).

bd.reimbursement: None; investigational. Autologous manufacturing implies per-patient logistics cost.
bd.notes: Microcap sponsor; financing risk is the main schedule variable.

name: EpiBone-CMF (EB-CMF) engineered living bone graft
composition: Patient-specific, CT-shaped decellularized bone scaffold seeded with the patient's adipose-derived stem cells and matured in a perfusion bioreactor

regulatory.reference: IND cleared May 2019 for a Phase 1/2 first-in-human study (NCT03678467); no BLA

applications.evidence_summary: Open-label, single-arm, six-patient first-in-human study of EB-CMF for mandibular ramus reconstruction (three US sites) registered with a 2021 start and August 2023 primary completion; the record was last updated May 2022 with status unknown, and no results have been published or presented in sources located as of 2026-10-22.
applications.caveats: Autologous cell-based combination product under FDA's cellular therapy pathway; funding rounds (Hackensack Meridian 2020, NetScientific) but no clinical readout; treat as stalled until a status update appears.

evidence.title: Open-label first-in-human single intervention study of EpiBone-CMF engineered living bone graft for mandibular ramus reconstruction
evidence.finding: Phase 1/2, status unknown since May 2022; no results posted.

pipeline.expected_milestone: No public milestone; ClinicalTrials.gov status unknown (record last verified May 2022).

bd.reimbursement: n/a
bd.notes: Only US tissue-engineered mandible construct to reach an IND; related academic programs (axially vascularized ceramic in Alexandria NCT04001842; ovine patient-matched permanent scaffolds, Nat Commun 2025) remain preclinical or non-US.

name: IDCT (rebonuputemcel; Injectable Discogenic Cell Therapy)
ownership_history: Private (Salt Lake City). Co-founder/CEO Flagg Flanagan announced retirement Oct 5, 2026 after 18 years; successor not named in release.
composition: Allogeneic, manufactured progenitor cell population derived from donated adult human disc tissue, delivered in a viscous (sodium hyaluronate) carrier by single intradiscal injection

regulatory.reference: IND; RMAT and Fast Track designations (company). FDA accepted Phase 3 protocols and manufacturing plan July 2024 (company). Not approved anywhere.

applications.evidence_summary: Phase 1/2 US trial (NCT03347708, n=60, 14 sites, saline- and vehicle-controlled) and a Japanese Phase 1/2 (NCT03955315, n=38, sham-controlled) completed Feb 2022; company reports favorable safety and pain/function signals. Pivotal Phase 3 DGX-A02 (NCT07254806, n=162, sham-controlled) dosing began Dec 2025/Jan 2026.
applications.caveats: Peer-reviewed publication of the Phase 1/2 efficacy data could not be located on PubMed during this review (unverified); early-phase trials were small; Phase 3 readout not before late 2027.

evidence.title: Randomized, double-blind, vehicle- and placebo-controlled Phase 1 of IDCT in single-level symptomatic lumbar disc degeneration (US)
evidence.finding: Completed (primary completion Feb 2022); 14 US sites; results not posted on ClinicalTrials.gov at review.

evidence.title: Randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled Phase 1/2 of IDCT in lumbar DDD (Japan)
evidence.finding: Completed Feb 2022; 6 sites.

evidence.title: DGX-A02: prospective, randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled, multicenter Phase 3 of IDCT in single-level mild-to-moderate lumbar disc degeneration
evidence.finding: Recruiting at 31 sites; started Dec 23, 2025; first patient treated Jan 2026; DSMB recommended continuation without modification June 9, 2026; primary completion Nov 2027 (52-week primary period, 104-week total).

pipeline.expected_milestone: Phase 3 primary completion Nov 2027 (ClinicalTrials.gov); no company guidance on BLA timing.

bd.reimbursement: None; investigational.
bd.notes: Private company; leadership transition Oct 2026 framed as preparation for late-stage development and potential commercialization.

name: Intradiscal / degenerative disc biologics (rexlemestrocel-L, IDCT, VIA Disc NP) - not fusion products
ownership_history: Mesoblast (ASX/NASDAQ: MESO), DiscGenics (private, Salt Lake City), VIVEX Biologics (private, Miami; VIA Disc NP is a 361 HCT/P nucleus pulposus allograft).
composition: Rexlemestrocel-L: allogeneic STRO-3+ mesenchymal precursor cells, 6 million cells with hyaluronic acid, single intradiscal injection. IDCT (rebonuputemcel): allogeneic discogenic progenitor cells in a viscous carrier. VIA Disc NP: processed allogeneic nucleus pulposus tissue reconstituted with saline.

regulatory.reference: Mesoblast: FDA IND, RMAT designation, BLA planned Q3 2027 after MSB-DR004 (NCT06325566). DiscGenics: Fast Track; phase 3 NCT07254806 started December 2025. VIVEX: VIA Disc NP marketed as a 361 HCT/P (not an approved therapy) while running an IND-stage RCT (NCT06778447).

evidence.title: Efficacy and safety of allogeneic mesenchymal precursor cells with and without hyaluronic acid for chronic low back pain: randomized, double-blind, concurrent-controlled 36-month study (MSB-DR003)
evidence.finding: Primary composite responder endpoint at 12 and 24 months not met in all subjects; MPC+HA reduced LS-mean pain vs saline at 12 and 24 months, with larger effects in patients with CLBP under 68 months; no treatment-related SAEs.

evidence.title: Rexlemestrocel-L + HA vs saline in moderate to severe chronic low back pain (MSB-DR004)
evidence.finding: Active, not recruiting; primary completion July 2027; company guides top-line mid-2027 and BLA Q3 2027.

evidence.title: IDCT (rebonuputemcel) vs sham in single-level mild-to-moderate lumbar disc degeneration (phase 3)
evidence.finding: Recruiting at 31 sites; primary completion November 2027; follows completed phase 1/2 NCT03347708 (n=60).

evidence.title: Nucleus pulposus allograft (VIA Disc NP) vs sham for lumbar discogenic pain
evidence.finding: Recruiting at 19 sites; primary completion October 2027; the earlier VIA Disc NP registry (NCT04652687) was terminated and a 500-patient registry 3.0 (NCT06345690) is active.

pipeline.expected_milestone: Mesoblast BLA Q3 2027 if MSB-DR004 succeeds; DiscGenics and VIVEX phase 3 readouts late 2027

bd.reimbursement: Not applicable; VIA Disc NP is billed today as a 361 tissue product in office/ASC settings with no established coverage.
bd.notes: Included only as context: these are injectables aimed at avoiding fusion, not fusion biologics. The first MSB-DR003 phase 3 missed its primary endpoint, which is why Mesoblast is running a second phase 3; VIA Disc NP's commercialization under 361 while in an RCT is a regulatory grey zone FDA has scrutinized for other 'structural tissue' allografts.

name: NVD-003 (autologous adipose-derived osteogenic 3D graft)
ownership_history: Spun out of UCLouvain (2013); FDA Orphan Drug and Rare Pediatric Disease designations for congenital pseudarthrosis of the tibia (December 2020), RMAT designation, IND (March 2021); Phase 3 in CPT started September 2025.
composition: Autologous adipose-derived stem cells differentiated into a scaffold-free 3D osteogenic implant with HA/beta-TCP particles (3M3 platform); manufactured per patient

regulatory.reference: IND (2021); Orphan Drug and Rare Pediatric Disease designations (2020); RMAT; eligible for a priority review voucher if approved
on_label_indications: Investigational: congenital pseudarthrosis of the tibia (pediatric, Paley type 3-4 diaphyseal); recalcitrant lower-limb nonunion in adults

applications.evidence_summary: Adult phase 1/2 in recalcitrant lower-limb nonunion (NCT06335394, n=11 enrolled, company reported 9 treated): clinical healing in 8/9 at 2 years, median 6 months, no implant-related complications (company release, December 2022). Pediatric CPT Phase 3 vs ICBG (NCT07112443, n=12, 7 sites US/EU, primary completion October 2026) is recruiting.
applications.caveats: Tiny uncontrolled adult series; company-reported; the Phase 3 is powered as an orphan study (n=12). Manufacturing is autologous and weeks-long, unsuited to acute trauma.
applications.challenge: Orphan CPT is a route to a BLA, not a trauma market; the adult nonunion path would need a separate pivotal.

applications.evidence_summary: Phase 1b/2a (NCT05693558; 17 patients: 9 adults with bone nonunion, 8 children with CPT) reported 88% healing at 12 months (100% where mechanical stability was achieved) in a January 2025 company release; a 12-patient randomized Phase 3 vs ICBG (NCT07112443) began Sept 2025 with the first two children implanted Feb-Mar 2026.
applications.caveats: Company-reported, not peer-reviewed; tiny n; Phase 3 is n=12 with a composite mRUST/clinical/no-secondary-intervention endpoint, acceptable only because the disease is rare.

applications.evidence_summary: Adult lower-limb nonunion cohort of the Phase 1/2: company reports 89% union at 24 months and no refractures at 5 years (April 2025 release). Adult critical-size-bone-defect Phase 3 in start-up (Sept 2026).
applications.caveats: Open-label, company-reported, small cohort; adult approval targeted 2031.

evidence.title: Phase 3 randomized controlled study of NVD003 vs iliac crest bone graft in pediatric congenital pseudarthrosis of the tibia
evidence.finding: Recruiting at Phoenix Children's, Loma Linda, Sinai Baltimore, Mayo, Brussels, Amiens, Barcelona; primary endpoint overall healing at 12 months (mRUST 13 or more, no pain on weight bearing, no secondary intervention).

evidence.title: Single-arm study of NVD-003 for recalcitrant lower limb nonunion in adults
evidence.finding: Active, not recruiting; company reported 8/9 clinical healing at 2 years.

evidence.title: NVD-003 in the treatment of congenital pseudarthrosis of the tibia (Phase 1b/2a, US/EU)
evidence.finding: Open-label; 12-month 'efficacy' 88% across 17 patients (9 adult nonunion, 8 pediatric CPT) per company release Jan 31, 2025; registry entry last verified Jan 2024.

pipeline.expected_milestone: Phase 3 primary completion October 2026, study completion July 2027 (ClinicalTrials.gov); BLA timing not public.

bd.reimbursement: Would be a biologic (BLA) with potential for separate payment; none today.
bd.notes: Sister product NVD-X3 (allogeneic) has an IND for cervical fusion (2024). The priority review voucher is the financial story.

name: NVDX3 (allogeneic adipose-derived osteogenic graft)
ownership_history: Same sponsor as NVD-003.
composition: Off-the-shelf allogeneic version of the Novadip 3M3 platform: adipose-derived cells differentiated into an osteogenic graft (details from company; scaffold composition not confirmed)

regulatory.reference: US IND for a Phase 2b/3 cervical spine fusion study cleared 2024-11-22 (company release). ClinicalTrials.gov lists three Novadip NVDX3 trials: NCT05961956 (low-grade degenerative lumbar spondylolisthesis, active not recruiting), NCT05987033 (distal radius fracture proof of concept, completed), NCT06532253 (long-term safety, recruiting, Luxembourg). No NCT for the US cervical Phase 2b/3 study was found.

applications.evidence_summary: Company reported 12-month Phase 1b/2a trauma results (Feb 20, 2025): durable bone union in 100% of distal radius fracture participants, no related adverse events.
applications.caveats: Company-reported, small open-label cohort; no NCT or publication located for the trauma or spine Phase 1b/2a studies during this review.

applications.evidence_summary: Interim first-in-human lumbar fusion data (Oct 2024, company): 90% of patients healing or progressing toward healing at 6 months. Phase 2b/3 in cervical fusion planned to enroll in the US from H2 2025.
applications.caveats: Interim, company-reported, no comparator; no registry entry located.

pipeline.expected_milestone: US cervical Phase 2b/3 start (IND cleared Nov 2024; enrollment target Nov 2025 per April 2025 release) not confirmed in any registry as of 2026-10-22.

bd.reimbursement: None; investigational.
bd.notes: An allogeneic, off-the-shelf osteogenic cell graft would compete directly with 361 cellular bone allografts but with a BLA and labeled claims; this is the strategically interesting asset in the Novadip portfolio.

challenge: No 2026 NVDX3 update or US cervical-study registration found.

name: Rexlemestrocel-L (MPC-06-ID; allogeneic STRO-3+ mesenchymal precursor cells with hyaluronic acid)
ownership_history: Developed by Mesoblast (Australia/US) since the 2011 Phase 2; no partner announced for the disc program as of Oct 2026.
composition: Immunoselected, culture-expanded allogeneic bone-marrow-derived mesenchymal precursor cells (6 million cells) mixed with hyaluronic acid carrier, single intradiscal injection

regulatory.reference: IND (number not public); RMAT designation for chronic low back pain due to DDD (company statements). No BLA filed as of Oct 2026.

applications.evidence_summary: Phase 3 MSB-DR003 (NCT02412735, n=404, 48 sites) did not meet its composite primary endpoint (50% VAS reduction plus 15-point ODI reduction at both 12 and 24 months without intervention); 36-month results published Spine J 2025 report pain and function improvements favoring cells over saline on secondary analyses. FDA's January 2026 Type B feedback (company account) is that pain-intensity effects favored rexlemestrocel-L and that a clinically meaningful 12-month pain reduction in the confirmatory trial could support efficacy.
applications.caveats: Sponsor-funded; primary endpoint of DR003 was missed; the BLA case rests on a single confirmatory trial (MSB-DR004, n=300, topline expected mid-2027). Bayesian responder analyses in DR003.

evidence.title: MSB-DR003: placebo-controlled Phase 3 of rexlemestrocel-L alone or with HA in chronic low back pain
evidence.finding: Primary composite responder endpoint (both 12 and 24 months) not met; results posted on ClinicalTrials.gov; 48 sites (47 US, 1 Australia), primary completion May 2020.

evidence.title: Efficacy and safety of allogeneic mesenchymal precursor cells with and without hyaluronic acid for treatment of chronic low back pain: a prospective, randomized, double blind, concurrent-controlled 36-month study (Spine J 2025; DOI 10.1016/j.spinee.2025.03.015)
evidence.finding: 36-month follow-up of the Phase 3; authors report durable reductions in pain and disability versus saline on secondary analyses (abstract truncated in retrieval; see notes).

evidence.title: Allogeneic mesenchymal precursor cells treatment for chronic low back pain associated with degenerative disc disease: a prospective randomized, placebo-controlled 36-month study (Spine J 2020; DOI 10.1016/j.spinee.2020.10.004)
evidence.finding: Phase 2 (NCT01290367): 6M and 18M MPC+HA vs HA vehicle vs saline at 13 sites, 3:3:2:2; safety and preliminary efficacy through 36 months supported the Phase 3 dose of 6 million cells.

evidence.title: MSB-DR004: randomized, double-blind, saline-controlled Phase 3 of rexlemestrocel-L + HA in moderate-to-severe chronic low back pain
evidence.finding: Started July 2024; 40 sites; recruitment target reached April 2026 and all 300 patients treated by August 2026 (company); 12-month pain endpoint; primary completion July 2027.

pipeline.expected_milestone: Topline from MSB-DR004 expected mid-CY2027; BLA filing targeted Q3 CY2027 if positive (Mesoblast releases Apr 29 and Aug 17, 2026). RMAT allows rolling review.

bd.reimbursement: None; investigational. Would be a physician-administered biologic (likely J-code) if licensed.
bd.notes: Mesoblast already holds a BLA for remestemcel-L (Ryoncil, pediatric GVHD, 2024), so it has a licensed MSC manufacturing platform. Commercial-scale manufacturing for the disc product is reportedly proceeding in parallel with DR004 (company).

name: Umbilical cord / Wharton's jelly / cord-blood injectables marketed for orthopedic use
company: Numerous; public FDA letters name New Life Medical Services (Restor+, Regain, Renyte), R3 Medical / Bello Bio / Regen Suppliers (ReBellaWJ, ReBellaCB), Dynamic Stem Cell Therapy; BioStem Life Sciences (Jan 2025, CGMP) per search results
ownership_history: Not applicable (class record).
composition: Minced, micronized or enzymatically processed umbilical cord tissue (Wharton's jelly) or cord blood, cryopreserved, sold as 'stem cell' injections; cell viability after processing is frequently near zero

regulatory.reference: FDA position: umbilical cord's basic function in the donor is a conduit between mother and fetus, so injection into a joint, disc or tendon is non-homologous (fails 1271.10(a)(2)); processing that disrupts the cord's tubular structure is more than minimal manipulation; allogeneic cord blood that depends on living cells fails criterion (a)(4). Products are unapproved new drugs (FD&C 505(a)) and unlicensed biologics (PHS 351(a)(1)). The only licensed cord-blood products are HPC, Cord Blood for hematopoietic reconstitution.

applications.evidence_summary: No controlled trial of any marketed umbilical cord injectable for bone healing; the New Life letter documents marketing for 'non-union fractures' and 'bone spurs' with no data.
applications.caveats: Sterility failures documented in multiple letters; CDC-investigated bacterial infections after cord-blood product injections (2018, Liveyon) are the safety precedent (not re-verified here).

evidence.title: FDA Warning Letter to New Life Medical Services, LLC (CBER 25-711102)
